artifact.supernaturalcraft.trait.mending: Your wounds close slowly on their own.
artifact.supernaturalcraft.trait.sixth_s: The hidden show themselves to you, as with Second Sight.
artifact.supernaturalcraft.trait.warding: Creatures' blows land a little softer (not a boss's).
artifact.supernaturalcraft.trait.whisper: Something whispers to you; your mind frays.
ash.supernaturalcraft.greet.0: Back again? Can't keep a good hunter away from a free bar.
ash.supernaturalcraft.greet.1: Hey! I was just recalibrating the jukebox. Whaddya need?
ash.supernaturalcraft.greet.2: Ah, my favourite dead regular. Well, mostly dead.
ash.supernaturalcraft.greet.3: Business in the front, party in the back. What can I do you for?
ash.supernaturalcraft.greet.first: Well, look who it is! Welcome to the Roadhouse, Heaven edition. Pull up a stool.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.hearth: Your house is yours now. Go sit by the hearth, you've earned it.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.homecoming: Miss the place? A little homecoming rite on Earth opens a gate right to your front door.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.memories: There are %s memories along your lane you haven't touched yet. Step through the veils.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.naomi: Your wing's open. Somebody named Naomi works in there. She's... not friendly. Take holy weapons.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.next_boss: Word down the wire is your next big one is %s.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.no_plot: You don't have a Heaven of your own yet. Open a gate of light back on Earth and walk through it.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.visits: %s Heavens out there would take a visitor. Want me to patch you through?
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.welcome: Your Heaven's closed to visitors. Say the word and I'll put you on the network.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.wing_sealed: That clinical wing in your Heaven? Sealed tight. Gather %s more memories and it'll open up.
ash.supernaturalcraft.hint.zachariah: Naomi's lift goes up to an office that never ends. Zachariah's been waiting. Bring your paperwork.
ash.supernaturalcraft.ramble.0: You ever notice Heaven runs on dial-up? I'm working on it.
ash.supernaturalcraft.ramble.1: Ellen says hi. Jo says you still owe her a beer.
ash.supernaturalcraft.ramble.2: Every Heaven is wired into one big network. I can see it all if I squint.
ash.supernaturalcraft.ramble.3: Nothing to report, chief. Grab a drink and enjoy the eternal afternoon.
block.supernaturalcraft.banner.men_of_le: Light blue Men of Letters Emblem
Light gray Men of Letters Emblem
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.abaddo: She shrugs off most blades. The First Blade bites her, and so does any hunter wearing the Mark. A devil's trap holds her a while; when she hides in a knight, exorcise her out, or salt the vessel.
She can only be hurt through her core: break the four rings, then the cysts at her roots. Keep her four wells burning and carry light; the dark eats you where you stand.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.azazel: Samuel Colt's iron still holds him. Call him up in a great circle at night and rails rise around it: he will not step inside. Knock him in, shoot him in, or stand behind the rails when he rushes you as smoke. Straight lines, always.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.broken: Break its faces, its wings and its wheels in turn. Meet no open eye, and hide in a pillar's shadow from its light. When it sings its Hymn, ring the bell it sings and it will kneel.
Nobody knows. Some say he lives in a cabin at the end of the world, and that the Fallen Star knows the way.
Offer him the three rings in a great circle, with the scythe. Keep hitting him: your clock winds back with every blow, or kill a reaper. When it runs out, run for the light.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.dick_r: Dick Roman, head of the Leviathans
Only a righteous man's bone, washed in the blood of the three, brings him to the table. Borax burns him and finds him when he wears your face; it dries his goo, too.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.famine: Call him with rotten flesh, bread, wheat and salt. Never eat near him: it feeds him. Kill his thralls before they reach him, and when he grabs a friend, all hit him at once.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.gabrie: He is no pagan god. Bait him at night with sweets inside a ring of holy oil. In TV Land play along: hit him when the audience stops laughing, stand on the right answer, strike on the beep, and in the commercial find the one who casts the shadow of six wings.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.grand_: Her shield is her sisters: crack their own shields and the channel breaks. When she takes everyone's taglock at once, stand where Rowena tells you.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.intro:
You asked for knowledge, so here's the useful kind.

The next thing standing between you and the top of the food chain: %s.

Turn the page.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.lilith: When she shines, put a headstone between you and her light; they crack, so move. If she writes your name, every blow against her pays the contract down. After each burst she is hollow for a moment: that is when to hit.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.lucife: Only holy things truly hurt him: angel blades, Smite, holy water. Everything he does is written on the ground first. Strike while he recovers; when he gathers his grace, stand in a green sigil or a Ward.
In the Cage at the heart of Hell, with the four rings and the Key. He is Lucifer and more: everything you learned still holds, but the floor will not. Keep moving.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.metatr: Write his name to call him. His Hand writes burning words on the floor: don't stand on them. When he speaks the Word from his lectern, obey it, to the letter.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.michae: Call him down by day with the Angel Tablet and the Seraph Wings, waking the circle with an angel blade. Never let his hand reach your brow. Strike down the Host's captain and the rest break. Say yes at your peril; when his halo breaks, pull his lance out of the ground and throw it back.
In the white wing of your own Heaven, once your memories have opened it. Never sit still near her chair; if she straps you in, struggle, and let a friend cut you loose. Spare the kneeling copies she raises.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.none:
You've killed everything worth killing. Congratulations.

The only thing left you should be afraid of is me.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.pestil: Call him with a fermented spider eye, mushrooms and clotted blood. Drink the antidote vials that turn up in his swamp, and burn his flies: fire aspect, a lighter, a burning block.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.raphae: Raphael, the archangel of the storm

Call him down in a thunderstorm, after the Horsemen. Pour no oil of your own: his house has rings of it. Wait till his hand goes up or he blinks into a ring, then light it; held in holy fire he can't strike or heal. Stand in his garrison's threads to cut them, and when he snaps his fingers, run to the green band.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.rowena: Kill her raven and her curses lose your scent. Free her hexed puppets with Break Hex or salt — killing them feeds her. When she floats and recites, smash her three bowls and she drops like a stone.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.title: What the Crossroads Know
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.war.we: Call him with swords, gunpowder and demon blood. Block his combos with a shield at the last moment and he staggers. Break his standards; under his spell, look for the demons who kneel and strike none of them, nor a friend.
book.supernaturalcraft.crossroads.zachar: In his office above your Heaven, up the lift from Naomi's room. File every form he hands you in its cabinet, or your blows are worth a quarter. What is written comes true: read the docket and stand where it isn't.
book.supernaturalcraft.hymn.page1: We were a choir of many, and we sang before the Throne. Then the Throne was empty, and our voices ran together, and we became one thing, and that thing is broken.
book.supernaturalcraft.hymn.page2: Above, on the summit, the seven bells wait. Bring the Shattered Hymn to the altar while the storm is overhead, and ring three notes.
book.supernaturalcraft.hymn.page3: Which three? The glass behind this book remembers. Read it as you read these pages: from left to right.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.anoint_the_: Washes the bone of a righteous mortal in the blood of the three: a fallen angel, a King of Hell and an Alpha. It is the only key to Dick Roman's door.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.banish_by_n: Sends the named away from afar: a ghost to rest, a demon to the dark, an angel home.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.bind_banish: Binds the nearest creature to the bowl, or sends demons, hounds and ghosts back where they came from.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.binding_of_: Roots the named to the spot, if they are within a few hundred blocks.
Burns a crossroads contract and takes back what was sold.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.break_hex.d: Lifts every curse from the named (or from you) and burns the curse bags near both.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.brew_bound_: Binds the poured blood to its owner, in a vial the strongest rites ask for.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.brew_chrism: Holy oil consecrated into chrism, which the great rites ask for.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.brew_hexed_: Steeps Enochian ink in one school: gold for Enochian, blaze powder for Infernal, amethyst for Witchcraft, salt for the Hunters.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.compel.desc: A creature follows you and will not raise a hand to you. A person named is drawn to the bowl.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.concealment: Hides you from demons, angels, hounds and spirits for three minutes. Never from the great ones.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.curse_of_fr: Strength drains away: weaker, slower to work, and every blow lands harder.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.curse_of_mi: Bad luck dogs whoever the bowl names: worse loot, weaker blows, a long jinx.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.curse_of_pa: Pain that comes and goes for a minute. Like poison, it never quite kills.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.curse_of_si: For a minute the named can neither cast a sigil nor call on their powers.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.familiar_bo: Binds a cat or parrot you tamed to you as a witch's familiar.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.find_the_au: The Fallen Star, ink, paper and holy water: the smoke draws a map to the one who wrote it all. Only for those who have beaten every great enemy.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.hex_bags.de: Binds a curse into a pouch to hide near an enemy, or a ward to carry against demons.
Hunger and sickness, and the food in their pack rots.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.locate.desc: Smoke drifts toward what you seek: a person by their blood, a pet by its collar, a place by a token of it.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.locate_bein: The smoke drifts toward whoever the bowl names, person or creature.
The next curse aimed at the named goes back to its caster.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.purificatio: Cleanses everyone near the bowl of curses and possession, burns hex bags and scatters ghosts. A variant breaks a crossroads deal.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.purified_bl: Human blood made holy: the demon cure, given a night at a time to a demon held in a devil's trap.
Calls a fallen pet back from the dark, by its collar.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.scrying.des: The smoke shows you where the named stands, and outlines them for a while.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.second_sigh: For three minutes you see what hides: ghosts, hellhounds, hidden hex bags.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.summon_cros: At night, anywhere: a crossroads demon steps out of the smoke beside the bowl, ready to deal. Bury nothing; just ask.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.summon_mess: Calls Heaven's messenger to a human free to choose, to offer Grace again. He never answers a demon.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.trace_the_f: The smoke leads to the nearest witch, or a witch's familiar.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.unmark.desc: Takes the Mark of Cain off whoever the bound blood names. Read from the Book of the Damned, by the witch who survived its keeper's choice, standing at the bowl.
bowl_spell.supernaturalcraft.ward_of_the: For ten minutes, curses aimed at the named fail and turn on whoever cast them.
Takes all your mana and gives it back quicker for good: each rite adds 1% of your bar a second.
%1$s kept watch in a Heaven garrison where no bell had ever sounded an alarm.
%1$s belonged to a choir charged with reciting orders that never explained their purpose.
Heaven set %1$s among the sentries of a sealed gate and forbade all questions about what lay beyond.
%1$s served in a garrison whose watch was measured in the rising and falling of mortal kingdoms.
The choir of %1$s sang the Father's will until silence became another order.
%1$s guarded Heaven's muster halls and learned every rank before seeing a human face.
%1$s came from a choir that carried decrees between Heaven's garrisons without changing a word.
%1$s stood in Heaven's reserve garrison, ready for a summons that took ages to arrive.
%1$s earned a post by holding a breach long after the order to withdraw had been lost.
%1$s was raised after returning every survivor of a broken garrison to the Host.
The Host promoted %1$s for carrying a judgement through without hesitation or witness.
%1$s earned command by preserving a line that older officers had called indefensible.
%1$s received a higher station after a century of watch with no breach and no complaint.
%1$s was appointed after exposing false orders sealed with a superior's own mark.
%1$s rose by taking the duties of a fallen commander before anyone ordered it.
%1$s earned the Host's trust by refusing an easy victory that would have broken formation.
The vessel of %1$s said yes after a long vigil beside a hospital bed.
%1$s wears the body of a believer who consented without asking what service would cost.
A weary soldier said yes to %1$s, hoping one last duty might mean something.
%1$s asked once, and the vessel answered yes with hands that would not stop trembling.
The person carrying %1$s consented in a roadside chapel with nobody else to hear.
%1$s found a willing vessel in someone who had spent a lifetime waiting for an answer.
The vessel said yes to %1$s on the condition that a loved one be allowed to leave unharmed.
%1$s received a whispered yes from a vessel who mistook solemnity for kindness.
%1$s was a human soul that learned, on Hell's rack, to mistake another's scream for relief.
The rack broke %1$s slowly, until the human soul begged to hold the knife instead.
%1$s entered Hell with a human name and left the rack without anything human to answer it.
Once human, %1$s counted years on the rack until numbers gave way to hunger.
%1$s kept one human memory through the rack, then traded it for a turn at the hooks.
Hell put the human soul of %1$s on the rack and made cruelty the only way off it.
%1$s learned every prayer as a human soul on the rack and every answer as a torturer.
The human soul called %1$s endured the rack until it began suggesting improvements.
%1$s climbed from the lowest ranks by selling a superior the names of three conspirators and inventing a fourth.
%1$s won a first promotion by returning with a rival's blade and no rival.
%1$s clawed upward through vacant posts that rarely became vacant by accident.
%1$s served every master just long enough to learn where each kept the knives.
%1$s earned a place above the rabble by collecting debts the collectors feared.
%1$s bought a first command with stolen souls, then killed the seller before the price rose.
%1$s rose one duel at a time and kept a tooth from every defeated superior.
%1$s made obedience look effortless while quietly removing everyone ahead.
%1$s stole a night watchman's body and still carries keys to doors long demolished.
The vessel %1$s wears was stolen from a traveller whose family still sets a place at supper.
%1$s took this body without permission and never learned its owner's favourite song.
%1$s stole a preacher's vessel and enjoys how easily strangers still trust its face.
This vessel belonged to a debt collector before %1$s seized it and widened the business.
%1$s stole a surgeon's hands and found less delicate work for them.
%1$s wears a stolen body whose wedding ring remains, mostly because it amuses the thief.
%1$s took a stranger's body at a lonely crossroads and left the stranger screaming inside.
chain.supernaturalcraft.backstory.fallen: %1$s fell after opening a gate for mortals the Host had ordered left outside.
%1$s asked why obedience required the burning of a village and would not accept silence.
%1$s followed a beloved superior into rebellion and found the promises already broken.
%1$s chose a mortal life over an unending watch and lost both in the choosing.
%1$s fell for refusing to surrender a willing vessel to punishment meant for its angel.
%1$s sold a Heaven secret to save a garrison and was condemned before the survivors returned.
%1$s mistook the silence above for permission to choose and learned otherwise too late.
%1$s fell after declaring that a broken order did not become holy through repetition.
chain.supernaturalcraft.backstory.hunter: %1$s grew up beside a road nobody took after dark.
%1$s learned the trade from a parent's unfinished journal.
%1$s survived a nest that left an entire town silent.
%1$s started hunting after a familiar face wore the wrong eyes.
%1$s once answered emergency calls, until one answered back.
%1$s found salt lines beneath the family home's new paint.
%1$s learned what walked at night on a stranded school bus.
%1$s inherited a car, a knife and a list of missing people.
%1$s held a salt line until the last family escaped.
%1$s earned a post by bringing a wounded patrol home.
%1$s took command when the radio went silent.
%1$s mapped the safe roads while stronger fighters argued.
%1$s kept an oath after everyone stopped paying for it.
%1$s survived three ambushes and taught the others how.
%1$s refused to leave a stranger behind in a burning nest.
%1$s won respect by admitting a mistake before it killed anyone.
%1$s wears a coat patched more often than it has been washed.
%1$s keeps a silver blade inside one battered boot.
%1$s has salt worked into every seam of an old jacket.
%1$s hides a shaking hand by checking the ammunition.
%1$s carries motel keys to rooms that no longer exist.
%1$s keeps a faded photograph behind an anti-possession charm.
%1$s has the stoop of someone who sleeps in parked cars.
%1$s smiles with one tooth replaced after a very bad exorcism.
chain.supernaturalcraft.backstory.leviat: %1$s remembers Purgatory before humans had names.
%1$s hunted in Purgatory where nothing ever stayed eaten.
Before the first city, %1$s knew only hunger and confinement.
%1$s came out of Purgatory with an appetite older than Hell.
%1$s remembers the Old Ones waiting behind a sealed world.
Purgatory taught %1$s that patience makes a larger meal.
%1$s heard the first rumours of escape and began counting mouths.
%1$s left the endless hunt for a world that could be farmed.
%1$s earned a seat by delivering a village without a single alarm.
The Board promoted %1$s after a rival became an operating expense.
%1$s turned a failed food line into the Board's most reliable herd.
%1$s secured the laboratories while the old management fought outside.
A shipment of hunters brought %1$s to the Board's attention.
%1$s climbed by making every superior's hunger somebody else's problem.
%1$s presented a rival's head as a proposal for restructuring.
The Board rewarded %1$s for expanding the Plan into hostile territory.
%1$s wears a consultant whose colleagues never noticed the change.
A missing auditor supplied %1$s with a face and access codes.
%1$s copied a food inspector and approved the next shipment.
The smile %1$s wears once sold insurance to frightened families.
%1$s took a manager's skin and kept the appointments in the diary.
A laboratory supervisor gave %1$s a face nobody questioned.
%1$s borrowed a buyer's face; the purchases became much larger.
%1$s chose a face already trusted with the village's food.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.betray: %1$s betrayed an old allegiance to serve %2$s.
%1$s abandoned a master and entered the service of %2$s.
%1$s turned from a former oath to follow %2$s.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.board_: The Board convened at SucroCorp and established a chain answerable to neither Heaven nor Hell.
From the SucroCorp penthouse, the Board declared the world open for acquisition.
The Leviathans founded their Board. To the new chain, every other faction was livestock.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.challe: %1$s demanded that %2$s answer in single combat.
%1$s called the hunter %2$s to answer in the ring.
%1$s demanded a duel with the hunter %2$s.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.champi: %1$s defeated %2$s in the duel of champions.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.coward: The hunter %2$s left the challenge of %1$s unanswered in cowardice.
%1$s named the hunter %2$s a coward for refusing the ring.
%1$s gained standing when the hunter %2$s failed to answer the challenge.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.crowne: %1$s ended the interregnum by taking the throne.
%1$s was crowned over the vacant seat.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.defeat: %1$s was struck down, though the end was uncertain.
%1$s fell without the certainty of a final killing.
%1$s was defeated and left a shadow of return.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.dick_f: %1$s, founder of the Board, was slain in his own penthouse. His chair awaited a successor.
The first Lord, %1$s, fell at the top of SucroCorp. The Board survived its founder.
%1$s was slain in his penthouse boardroom; the founder's place at the table stood empty.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.duel_d: %1$s killed %2$s in a duel to the death.
%1$s ended a lethal duel with the death of %2$s.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.duel_w: %1$s won the trial of arms against %2$s.
chain.supernaturalcraft.chronicle.duel_y: %1$s forced the surrender of %2$s in the ring.

cinematic.supernaturalcraft.uncaged.phas: Every soul down here burned once. Now it is your turn.
Do you know how cold it gets in there?
Kill the hounds, or they will drag you down.
Watch for gold on the ground. The stars are falling.
Stand between the wings. When he burns, find the green.

cinematic.supernaturalcraft.war.mount.su: "Look at you. You can't even get your own people to stop fighting."

deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.ascend.0.des: The weapon in your hand, one Ascension higher. No shard, no forge, no sweat.
Maps to what hides nearby: a Hymnal Spire, a restless grave. Or, failing that, how to kill what you fear next.
A little something from my pockets. Bullets, embers, shards, diamonds... you'll see.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.recover.0.de: Everything from your last death that nobody picked up. Lava, void, time: none of it stops me.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.recover.1.de: The pet you lost, back on its feet and wagging. Don't ask where it's been.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.revive.0.des: Your last dead pet, on its feet. Even if there was nothing left of it. Especially then.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.0.des: The Yellow-Eyed Demon, in stone, eyes and all, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.1.des: The first demon, carved white and smiling, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.10.de: Heaven's reprogrammer, drill at rest, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.11.de: Heaven's middle manager, stamped and filed, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.12.de: The Darkness, caught in a sliver of light, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.13.de: The pale rider. Don't look it in the eye, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.14.de: The Sword of Heaven, finally holding still, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.15.de: The Father of Murder, a bee on his collar, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.16.de: The Knight of Hell, smiling as if she knows something you don't, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.17.de: Rowena MacLeod in green stone, one eyebrow raised forever, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.18.de: The Grand Coven's matriarch, her crystal still faintly lit, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.2.des: The Devil's own likeness. He'd be flattered, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.3.des: The Trickster, mid-grin, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.4.des: The red rider, mounted on your wall, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.5.des: The hungry one, at last with nothing to eat, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.6.des: The sick one, wiped down. Mostly, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.7.des: The archangel of the storm, still crackling, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.8.des: What is left of the Broken Chorus, humming, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.trophy.9.des: The Scribe of God, quill behind his ear, and one of the shards it left. I keep a collection.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.uncurse.0.de: Every hungry weapon you carry, fed to bursting. For now.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.uncurse.1.de: Heaven loses your number. Not my problem if they find it again.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.uncurse.2.de: That hollow feeling? Gone. Temporarily filled with something of mine.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.uncurse.3.de: Whoever hexed you, their bag is now a bag of nothing.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.upgrade.0.de: Two more hearts, yours for good. Hard to kill, harder to collect.
deal.supernaturalcraft.wish.upgrade.1.de: Twenty-five more mana, yours for good. Spell away.

PATIENCE IS A VIRTUE. SO IS COMPLIANCE.
EVERYTHING HAPPENS FOR A REASON. THE REASON IS ON FILE.
%1$s. The one who finished the book. I've been rereading it - you have no idea how rare a good ending is.
You want another draft, don't you? Of course you do. Nobody ever likes the ending they get.
Well? Ask. Or don't. I'll write it either way.
Back again. I kept your page warm.
What else do you want to know? I've got time. I've got all of it, actually.
My sister. Before there was a page, there was her, and the dark was the whole book.
I locked her away so I could write. That's what you do with family who won't let you work.
You stood under her eclipse and lived. She doesn't let many people do that. Maybe she likes you. She was always the sentimental one.
We made up, sort of. Then we didn't. Siblings. There's a lot of that in my work.
Another draft? Of course. Nothing is ever finished, only abandoned.
Same chapters, same rules. I won't give you anything for it this time - the props department is closed.
Say you're ready, and I'll put in a fresh sheet.
Oh. Hi. Come in, come in - mind the bottles. I was just finishing a chapter.
You found me. Honestly, %1$s, I wasn't sure you would. Most of my characters never look up from the page.
Sit anywhere. Not the chair by the desk. That one's mine.
So. You have questions. Everybody has questions at the end. Go ahead.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.lucife: My son. My most beautiful, most disappointing son.
He wanted me to love him more than I loved my story. I tried. I really did. Then I wrote the Cage.
You put him back in the box. Twice, if we're counting drafts. He'll tell you it wasn't fair. He's right. Fair was never the genre.
If he ever asks about me, tell him I said hi. He'll hate that.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.monste: Why the monsters? Why does anyone write monsters?
Conflict, %1$s. Without something in the dark, a hunter is just a person with a lot of salt. You'd have stayed home. Nobody reads that.
The great enemies were the act breaks. Azazel to get you moving, Lilith to raise the stakes, the Devil for the midpoint. The rest was escalation. You can't open with the Darkness.
Every one of them thought they were the main character. That's the trick. So did you.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.not_ye: No? That's fine. That's fine. I can wait. I'm very good at waiting.
Take your time. It's mine anyway.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.option: Why the monsters? Why any of it?
Ready. Everybody says that. Nobody ever is.
All right, %1$s. Chapter One. Try to keep up.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.story_: Your story's over, %1$s. I typed "The End" myself. You have the manuscript - read it sometime. I think you come off well.
Everything after this is fan fiction. I don't mind. I read it.
But if you want to go back in, the door's right there. It's always right there.
Your story. Let me find the page... there. The gun.
You picked up the Colt, %1$s. Of course you did. Everyone thinks the gun that can kill anything is the clever part.
Who do you think wrote the gun? It can kill almost anything. I'm not on the list. I'm not even on the page the list is written on.
Keep it, though. It's a good prop.
Your story? I know it. I wrote it. Let's see... ah, yes. The crossroads.
You made a deal, %1$s. A soul for a little something. The dogs, the clock, the kiss. Classic. I almost cried.
People think deals are about desperation. They're about plot. Nothing moves a character faster than a debt.
I didn't make you do it, by the way. I just made sure the crossroads was there when you walked by.
Your story, %1$s? It's a good one. Not great. Good.
A hunter with a journal and a handful of salt, walking into every dark room I left open. You took notes. I appreciated that. Most people skim.
You killed what I put in front of you, and you put the big ones down in the order I planned - or close enough that I could pretend.
The middle dragged a little. That's on me.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.who.0: Chuck. Chuck Shurley. Writer, mostly. A little guitar. People call me other things, but that gets awkward at parties.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.who.1: I wrote the books. The prophet's books, the Winchester gospels - and this. The salt, the sigils, the bowl, the Hell you walked through. All of it was a first draft once.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.who.2: You're thinking, "that's a lot of power for a man in a bathrobe." It is. The bathrobe is comfortable. I earned it.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.who.3: Don't worry, I'm not angry. Being angry would mean something had surprised me.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.author.winche: Ah. Sam and Dean. My favourites. Don't tell anyone.
Two brothers in a beautiful old car, saving people, hunting things. Fifteen seasons - years. Fifteen years of the best material I ever had.
And then they stopped doing what I wrote. Free will. It's adorable, until it isn't.
You remind me of them a little. Same bad diet, same refusal to stay dead. Let's see if you have the same problem with endings.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.again: You again. The bees are calmer than you are. Say what you came to say.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.again.ho: Could I have some of that honey?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.hello: Easy. You'll upset the bees, and they don't take to strangers any better than I do. You've come a long way to find an old man with a smoker. So. Who sent you?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.hello.ho: Could I have some of that honey?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.honey: Here. From the east hives. It's good for the throat — and for other thirsts, if you ever have the misfortune.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.honey.ho: Could I have some of that honey?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.mark: The Mark. Everyone who finds me wants to talk about the Mark. It isn't a gift. It's a curse that wants to be fed — kill, and it quiets; stop, and it gnaws at you until you're something else.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.no_honey: One jar a day. The bees work hard, and so should you.
Could I have some of that honey?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.not_read: You haven't seen enough of Hell to know what you're asking for. Go put the Devil back in his cage first.
Could I have some of that honey?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.not_toni: Not with the sun up. Not in front of the hives. Come back when it's dark, and we'll see what you're made of.
Could I have some of that honey?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.refuse: No. I won't hand it to you. I've seen what it does. If you want it that badly, you'll have to prove you can carry it — and that means getting past me.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.who: My name is Cain. Yes, that Cain. I killed my brother to save his soul, and I killed a great deal more after, as the first Knight of Hell. Then I met a woman named Colette, and I put down the blade. Now I keep bees. It's quieter.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain.who.hone: Could I have some of that honey?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain_mark.gra: The earth over Cain's grave is warm. Something under it is waiting — the Mark, for whoever beat him.
Put your hand on the earth. Take the Mark.
The earth over Cain's grave is warm. The Mark was taken off you once; it has not forgotten you. Take it again and it comes back thirsty — it remembers the way.
Put your hand on the earth. Take it back.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.cain_mark.off: "You beat me. Then it's yours, if you want it — the Mark, and everything it costs. Think hard. Once it's on you, it doesn't come off."
No. Let it die with him.
Take his arm. Take the Mark.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.grand_witch.h: So. The redhead is finally dead, and by a hunter's hand. The Grand Coven pays its debts: show me that Book, give me your blood, and I'll burn that ugly Mark off your arm.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.grand_witch.n: The cure must know whose Mark it unmakes. A vial of your own bound blood — the bowl can make it, if you know how.
And read it from what, my memory? Bring the Book of the Damned. You kept it; carry it.
You bear no Mark. The Coven's debt is paid — for now.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.grand_witch.s: I have no business with you, hunter. Walk away while I still find you dull.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.grand_witch.u: It is done. The Book is still yours — keep it close, and keep it away from anyone like her.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.lucifer_offer: A demon. One of my children, come to kill me? Kneel instead. Serve me, and I will make you a prince of the world to come.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.messenger.gre: I am a messenger of the Lord. You have done Heaven a service, hunter: the Yellow-Eyed Demon is dead. I was sent to make you an offer.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.messenger.off: This is Grace. Take it to an altar by day, in a circle of white candles, with an angel's blade, and you will be one of us. It is a war, hunter. We could use you.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.again: Back again? I'm flattered. Mildly. What is it this time, darling?
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.book_a: Is that... the Book of the Damned? In your grubby hands. Oh, darling. That Mark on your arm will eat you alive, and the only cure in all creation is written in those pages — in a language only a witch like me can read. Give it to me and I'll take the Mark off you. Think carefully: whatever you choose, there's no taking it back.
Take it. Help me get this Mark off. (Final)
No. The Book stays with me. (Final)
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.book_g: Wise. Wiser than you look. Now listen: the moment the Grand Coven learns I have this, they'll come for it — and for me. Their Grand Witch has wanted me dead for three hundred years. Call them out before they choose the time, and I'll stand with you. Then the Mark comes off. You have my word, such as it is.
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.book_k: Then you're a fool, and a fool with something of mine. Run along to the Grand Coven if you like — they'll love you. And when you're ready to die, read that Book in my house at night. I'll be waiting.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.bought: Pleasure doing business. Read it somewhere I can't see you mispronounce it.
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.clue: So you put the Devil back in his box. Impressive, for a hunter. Very well: Cain. The Father of Murder keeps bees now, if you can believe it — a little farm out where the roads give up, honey and silence. Mind the bees. Mind him more.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.clue.b: About the Book of the Damned...
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.clue.c: How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.clue_a: I told you already. Bees, a farm, the end of the roads, and the oldest killer there is. Do keep up.
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.coven: The Grand Coven answers a proper rite: a great circle, the blood bound to you, ink steeped in witchcraft, amethyst, a ghast's tear and a candle, at night — and my card to call them by. Their Grand Witch will come with three of her sisters channelling into her. Break the channel, and she bleeds like anyone.
About the Book of the Damned...
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.hello: Well, well. A hunter on my doorstep, and not even the decency to bring flowers. Rowena. Rowena MacLeod. You've heard of me, surely — everyone worth knowing has. Wipe your boots.
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.hostil: You. You have some nerve, standing in my house with my Book. Get out — or read it here after dark, and we'll settle this properly.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.lesson: Pick a page. I'll copy it out for you myself — and you'll pay what it's worth, not what you think it's worth.
Something else.

dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.needs_: I'm a witch, not a miracle worker. Bring me a vial of your own bound blood — the spell has to know whose Mark it's tearing off.
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.no_les: Nothing I'd trust you with yet. Come back when your witchcraft is less embarrassing, or when you've earned a little more of my good will.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.sold: There. Try not to curse yourself with it.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.sold.b: About the Book of the Damned...
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.sold.c: How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.too_po: Oh, sweetheart. You can't afford me. Come back with the full price — I don't haggle with people who still say 'magic' like it's a card trick.
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.unmark: There. Gone. Don't look at me like that — I keep my bargains. Mostly. The Mark won't come back unless you're stupid enough to take it again.
About the Book of the Damned...
How do I call the Grand Coven?
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.wares: Taglocks for whoever you'd like to ruin, and ink steeped properly, unlike the swill the hedge witches sell.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.who: The most gifted witch you will ever meet, and I've met the competition. Three hundred years of practice, a Grand Coven that threw me out for being better than them, and a house I keep far nicer than you keep anything. I teach. For a price. Everything is for a price.
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.who.bo: About the Book of the Damned...
dialogue.supernaturalcraft.rowena.who.co: How do I call the Grand Coven?

Consecrates the ground around the altar
Curses whoever the bowl names
Takes your whole bar: +50 mana, or quicker mana, for good
Tears a rift home, to your bed
Casts out every trapped demon nearby, leaving hellfire embers.
Makes a tamed pet your familiar
Forges a Guild Standard
Opens a gate of light to the door of your home in Heaven
Smoke drifts toward the one you seek
Draws a map to the nearest Hymnal Spire, high in the mountains.
Sews a hex bag
Guards a name against curses
Opens a gate of light into your own Heaven
Tears a rift into Hell behind the altar
Cleanses curses, possession and spirits nearby
Brings a dead pet back by its collar
Shows where the named stands
Calls up Abaddon, Knight of Hell
Calls the Darkness down. Only under an eclipse.
Calls up Azazel, the Yellow-Eyed Demon
A crossroads demon answers
Calls up Death, the Pale Rider (gives back the rings either way)
Calls Dick Roman to his boardroom
Calls up Famine, the Black Rider
Baits the Trickster into TV Land
Calls up Lilith, the First Demon
Opens the Cage.
Opens the Cage: Lucifer Uncaged
Calls Heaven's messenger
Calls down Metatron, the Scribe of God
Calls down Michael, the Sword of Heaven (gives back the relics either way)
Calls up Pestilence, the Pale-Green Rider
Calls Raphael down into the storm
Calls up War, the Red Rider
Takes the Mark of Cain off the named
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.angel_tablet: Dropped by Metatron. Once Lucifer has fallen, write "Metatron" in a book and quill and call him down at night in a great circle with it, two choir shards, two holy water, two feathers and a glow ink sac.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.antidote_vial: Turns up in the swamp while Pestilence fights. Drink it to cure the plague and keep it off for fifteen seconds.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.ascension_sha: At the Hellforge, with a weapon (or Hunter's Gear, or the General's armour) and this shard of the next tier: Ascend for 5 levels per tier. Shard I comes from a rite; the great enemies leave the rest.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.azazel_blood: Dropped by Azazel, two vials every time he falls. The Key to the Cage is forged with it. Call him up at night with a great circle, three demon blood, three sulfur and two salt, lit with flint and steel.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.chorus: Found on the summit of a Hymnal Spire. Lay a Shattered Hymn on the Choir Altar in a thunderstorm, then ring the hymn's three notes on the bells: the temple window on the stair shows them, left to right. Creative players can read an altar's hymn with an empty hand, or sneak and ring three bells to set it.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.colt: One round of the Colt kills any living thing outright, except players, the great enemies and archangels and those above them. A great enemy takes a tenth of its full strength that nothing blunts (the Author under a third of that; it still stops at each phase); an archangel, a heavy blow. Five chambers, loaded one round at a time: sneak-use or [R]. Its rounds cannot be crafted: forge them by night in a blood circle, eight at a time, once you have held the Colt; a few lie in the Hymnal Spire's temple and with the fallen bosses.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.death_clock: In Death's fight every hunter carries a clock of about a minute. Hit him, or kill a reaper, to wind it back. When it runs out you fall into limbo: reach the light in fifteen seconds or die.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.fallen_star: Dropped by Lucifer Uncaged. The rarest thing there is; its use is still to come.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.hell_material: Found in Hell: brimstone in the Ash Wastes, hooks on the Rack, contracts in Crowley's Corridors, shards in the walls of the Pit, fangs from hellhounds.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.hellforge: Place a weapon and runes, then Grave (tier x 2 levels per rune). Purge returns the runes but one, lost at random (1 level). With an Ascension Shard of the next tier in the leftmost slot, Ascend raises the weapon (or Hunter's Gear, or the General's armour) one tier.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.horseman_stee: Left behind by a Horseman every time he falls: a better horse than any you could breed. Tame it, saddle it and ride it like any other.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.horsemen_trop: Left behind by a Horseman every time he falls.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.hound_whistle: Dropped by Lilith. Blow it to call a hellhound to your side for a minute.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.last_seal: Dropped by Lilith. The last of the sixty-six seals: Lucifer's summoning needs it. Once Azazel has fallen, call her up at night in a great circle with three demon blood, two hellfire embers, two bones and a sheet of paper, lit with flint and steel.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.michael: Michael, the Sword of Heaven, is called down by day in a great circle in the Overworld, once Metatron has fallen: offer the Angel Tablet, the Seraph Wings, three choir shards and two holy waters, and wake it with an angel blade. He gives the relics back, win or lose.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.plague: Pestilence's plague stacks up to five times: each stack eats at you, takes a heart of max health and stops natural healing. Only his antidote cures it.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.rings: The Rings of the Four Horsemen. Each is won from its Horseman: call up War, Famine and Pestilence by their rites once Lucifer has fallen, then offer their three rings in a great circle to call up Death. Laid together on the dais under Lucifer's Cage, at the heart of the Pit, the four open it.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.runes: Carved from a blank rune at a small circle. Each fits weapons, catalysts or both; at most two alike on one weapon. The Void rune takes a tier IV weapon.
jei.supernaturalcraft.info.void_essence: Left behind by the Darkness. Carve it into a Void rune.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.artifa: A %2$s, %3$s. The order has worked out what it does.
No curse could be found on it. That is rare.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.case:
Case No. %s: %s

The suspect: %s. %s

The site: X %s, Z %s. Danger: %s.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.case.u: Not yet written up: a desk will take it as research.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.case.w: Written up and filed in the archive.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.creatu: The order's file on %s, level %s. What you know of it makes you %s%% deadlier against it.
How %s moves: where it comes from, when it is about, how fast it closes.
Where %s is weak: the joints and the angles a blade finds first.
How %s fights: its tells, the moment before it strikes.
What %s fears, and what it ignores.
Accounts from the old files: hunters who met %s and lived to write it down.
Everything else the order has on %s. The rest is up to you.
The order has no file on %s yet. A research desk will open one once you have notes enough.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.effect: It lays an effect on whoever the smoke finds.
It works as a rite of the altar would, from the bowl.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.formul:
A formula of the order, worked from %2$s. Tier %3$s; it costs %4$s mana and rests %5$s seconds after use.

Its words, changed: %6$s.
It is in your grimoire now: compose it in the scriptorium like any sigil you know.
Every note you take in the field is filed here, not carried: what you saw, what died and how. Research at a desk is paid out of these.
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.rite:
Pour: %2$s.

Then add what is shown below, light the bowl and recite:
"%3$s"

It costs %4$s mana. %5$s
journal.supernaturalcraft.archive.rite.u: The bowl knows this rite now, as it knows the ones on the old spell pages.
The last Knight of Hell, the one Cain did not finish. She does not come unless called: a great circle by night in the Overworld, once Cain and three of the Horsemen (War, Famine and Pestilence) have fallen to you, with the First Blade to wake it (it is not spent).

Most blades barely touch her: she takes about a third of every blow. The First Blade lands in full, and so does every blow of a hunter who bears the Mark of Cain. A devil's trap holds her for six seconds, every blow landing in full; then she tears it apart, and for half a minute no trap will hold her.

The Knight of Hell: her herald marks a hunter with a red circle that follows them, stops, and burns, and her knights run at the spot; a sweep of hellfire before her; her retinue called back when it falls.

Possession: her body turns to smoke and dives into one of her knights. Her smoke cannot be struck, but the knight's wounds are hers. Drive her out (the Exorcise sigil, Salt Shot, Banish by Name with her taglock or the knight's, the knight dragged onto a devil's trap, or the knight killed) and she is thrown back into her body, stunned for five seconds and taking twice the harm. Left alone she comes out by herself after sixteen.

The Brand of the Knights: a telekinetic grip that holds whoever stays in its violet circle for two seconds, and the Brand itself, three red rings round her, each broken by two green gaps. Stand in a gap, or between the rings.
What she leaves: the Book for everyone who fought her; the cleaver and her bust the first time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.abaddon_: A robed demon with a bell. He keeps his distance and rings it at a hunter: a red circle follows them for a second and a half, holds still, then burns, and the knights come running at the spot. Keep moving, and step out once it stops. Now and then he calls fire down at someone's feet.
Only one at a time serves her. Kill him first.

Demons in blackened plate who rise out of hellfire round her, two at a time, three at most. A knight's slash sweeps a wide arc before him. Strike him from the front and he may raise his shield: while it is up, blows from the front glance off. Go round him.
When Abaddon rides one he glows from inside, hits harder, moves faster and never raises his shield; his wounds are hers. When she falls, her knights crumble with her.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.abandone: Out on the plains, in the forests and the taiga, snow or none, stand ruined chapels nobody prays in any more: rotten pews, a broken altar, a bell tower, and a crypt under the floor.

Their chests keep sigil pages, Enochian and Hunter, of the first three tiers, with holy water, salt, candles and now and then chrism. Their quiet does not always hold: a ghost haunts about a third of them, and a hexed villager or two about a quarter.
A church can be cleansed: see Consecrate Church, among the rites.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.against_: Carry light, for the dark eats you where you stand. Torches, lanterns, the censer's beam and smiting light all count. She will snuff what you place; light it again.
When the Totality comes, stand by a burning well. When the ground is unmade, stand in the light.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.allegian: Where each road begins. Heaven: defeat Azazel and wait for the dawn, when its messenger comes to offer you Grace (see The Angel's Road). Hell: call a crossroads demon with the bowl (Summon a Crossroads Demon) and ask for "Make me one of you", or tick "Bind my soul" on any deal and let the hounds take you when it falls due (see The Demon's Road). The hunter's road: swear the Hunter's Oath at the altar (see Rites of the Road).

Every hunter starts human, and free. Heaven may send for you, Hell may bargain for you, or you may stay what you are. An angel climbs four ranks (Lesser Angel, Seraph, Archangel, General of the Host), a demon four more (Crossroads Demon, Prince of Hell, Knight of Hell, King of Hell); each rank is a rite at the altar, paid for with what the great enemies leave behind. The fourth road of the roadmap follows all three branches.

A side has its own strength: Grace for an angel, Corruption for a demon, in a ring around the emblem beside your mana. The bar holds 100 at the first rank, then 150, 200 and 250. Hold V to open the wheel of your powers and point at one, let go to choose it, and press B to use it on whatever you are looking at. Passive gifts work on their own. Every rank, on any road, also deepens your mana by 25 (125 at the first, up to 200 at the fourth), so that each rite can be paid at the rank before it.

Choosing has a price. Holy things burn what you have become, monsters of your side leave you alone and the other side hunts you, and so do other hunters. Your eyes give you away when you use your powers. A human keeps their free will: no possession takes them, Heaven cannot mark them, and Michael never asks them for their yes. All their magic, sigils, bowl spells and rites alike, costs 15% less mana, and they are given longer to recite at the bowl.

The way back costs too: a demon can be cured over three nights, an angel can have their Grace cut out. Either way you are human again, without your ranks, and must wait three days before choosing a side once more.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.amara.0: The Darkness, God's sister, before the light. Only under an eclipse, in the Overworld, in a void circle lit with a nether star: two echo shards, two eyes of ender, two demon blood, a black candle and dragon's breath.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.amara.1: She cannot be hurt but through her core. First break the four rings that circle her, then three of the cysts at her roots, and each time she sinks with her core laid open: strike it. Then the Black Sun, core open, and at the last, her own body.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.amara.2: Four wells of holy fire stand at the points of her ground. Each one burning weakens her; she will put them out, and you light them again. Holy strikes and light on her core count most.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.amara_sh: Small echoes of the Darkness that hunt in the dark around her. Light burns them, and strong light unmakes them outright: torches and lanterns set down, the censer's beam, a burning well.
Fight them where it is bright and they are no trouble. Let the dark close in and they come in numbers. The Colt kills one with a single round, if you can spare it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angel_bl: The angel blade: a diamond sword, a chrism, a holy water, two gold ingots and a hellfire ember, in a binding circle. Hold use, then let go, and you dash through your enemies in a line of light. You will know it is ready: the engravings wake and the whole blade burns white in your fist, held point down, the way they hold it.
The exorcist's mace: an iron block in place of the sword. It may stun what it hits, and brought down from a height it sends out a ring of holy force.
Both are holy. Both are tier II. Both are what you want in your hand the first time you open the Cage.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angel_ch: Its hymn mends every angel around it and rings in the ears of its enemies. Kill it first, or the fight never ends.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angel_do: Slow, towering and armoured, it does not blink like the others. When it lifts its hammer high, get out of the way: the judgement lands all around it.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angel_he: Heaven's messengers still carry spears, only now they are made of light. It keeps away and throws them, straight and fast. Cover is your friend.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
A herald, a lance of light in hand
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angel_pa: How to begin. There is no spell for it: Heaven has to come to you. Defeat Azazel, the Yellow-Eyed Demon, and at the next dawn an angel in a trench coat finds you wherever you are in the Overworld. Hear him out and take what he offers: a Vial of Grace, and the page to call him again (the bowl spell Summon the Messenger). Turned away, he comes back three dawns later.

Then raise the rite Receive Grace: a ritual altar inside a grace circle (a ring of chalk with four lit white candles, north, south, east and west, two blocks from the altar), by day, in the Overworld. Lay the Vial of Grace, two holy waters and four gold ingots on it and light it with an Angel Blade, which you keep.

Lesser Angel. Receive Grace by day in the Overworld: the Vial of Grace, two holy waters and four gold ingots, with an Angel Blade to raise it. Teleport where you look, heal with a touch, draw an angel blade from your sleeve, and listen to Angel Radio: for a while, demons and bosses within 128 blocks whisper where they are. Wipe the memories of everything near: for a while nothing remembers it was fighting you.

Seraph. A Damned Contract, three choir shards and the Seraph Wings: your own wings, folded at rest and open in flight, carry you for as long as their strength lasts. Smite: a palm to the face of what you look at. Holy chains bind what you look at in place.

Archangel. By day, Lucifer's Grace and an Archangel Blade. Your wings turn to light and you can show your true form for ten seconds: every demon that sees it burns, and the light blinds the rest. A snap of your fingers and the lesser foes near you burst.

General of the Host. Michael's Grace and a Fallen Star, with Michael's Lance in hand: a captain and four soldiers of the Host answer you for a minute, and you can hurl lances of light. Call a pillar of judgment down where you look, and ascend to your plot of Heaven with the friends who kneel beside you (from Heaven, the same takes you all back down).
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angel_ta: The word of God, cut in stone, taken from Metatron still burning. Use it and it rewrites your story: healed whole, every harm undone, the fire put out.
It needs two minutes before it will write again. Save it for the moment you would otherwise not walk away.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angel_te: A soldier of the Host with a tower shield. While it is raised, blows from the front barely land; go round it. Up close its sword cuts wide.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
A templar of the Host behind its shield
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.angels_o: Lilith was the last seal. Since she fell, Heaven has sent its own down to walk among us: men and women in borrowed bodies, a blade up the sleeve, a light behind the eyes. You only see their wings as a shadow, when they strike or when they are suddenly somewhere else.
They leave a hunter be, unless you start it. Hell's sworn they hunt on sight, and the fallen, and every demon they find. To one of Heaven's own they are brothers and sisters.
Anything will hurt one, a little. Only an angel blade will truly kill it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.archange: Lucifer's own blade, left when he falls. Holy, deadly to demons, and tier IV.
Use it and it smites everything in a cone before you, for a price in mana.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.archive_: The last of the Knights of Hell, Cain's own lieutenants. A Man of Letters trapped her in 1958 and lost her head to her; the order's files on her end there. She wears her vessels like coats.

Tactical note: Most blades barely mark her; the First Blade and the Mark of Cain bite in full, and a devil's trap holds her. When she hides inside one of her knights, exorcise or salt the vessel and she is thrown out reeling.
Abaddon, Knight of Hell
God's sister, locked away before creation, older than anything the order could name.
Tactical note: Light is the weapon: fight from the lit wells and keep them lit.
Amara, the Darkness
A Prince of Hell, the first of Lilith's children, who led the demons that hunted special children. The order's file on him runs to three volumes and stops in 1958.
Tactical note: His smoke dash runs in a straight line: lay the Colt's rails in his path and let him run into the trap.
Azazel, the Yellow-Eyed Demon
Not one angel but many, fused into a single singing thing in a spire nobody built. The order heard of it only in a hymn.
Tactical note: Its gaze charges before it strikes: put a column between you and its eyes.
The Broken Chorus

The first murderer, who killed Abel to keep his brother's soul out of Hell and took the Mark from Lucifer in exchange; the first Knight of Hell. The order lost track of him in the 1950s; the last entry says he keeps bees.
Tactical note: Only at night, in his yard. When the Mark flares, run for the green shelters by his hives; his own First Blade bites him hardest.
Cain, the Father of Murder
God, who wrote everything, including the order, and this file.
Tactical note: In the light he can only be hurt when a window opens: find it, and disobey the narration when he tells you not to.
The Author
The oldest of the Four, who will one day reap God himself. The order never wrote a file on him; they wrote him letters.
Tactical note: Every blow you land winds your clock back. Never stop hitting him.
Death

The order's last file on the Leviathans is from 1958: a note that they were sealed in Purgatory before the first word was written, and a tablet fragment no one could read. Now one of them runs a company.
Tactical note: Borax burns him and finds him when he wears a hunter's face; it dries his goo into somewhere to stand. He only answers the bone of a righteous mortal washed in the blood of the three.
Dick Roman, Roman Enterprises
The Horseman of hunger, an old man in a wheelchair who feeds on what people crave.
Tactical note: Do not eat near him: it feeds him. Kill his thralls before he does.
Famine
The archangel who ran away from his family's war and hid among the pagan gods as Loki. He likes a joke, and a joke's victim.
Tactical note: Each channel has its rules. Learn the rule first, then fight: the real Gabriel is the one with the shadow of wings.
Gabriel, the Trickster
The matriarch of the Grand Coven, the oldest circle of witches in the Old World. The order traded letters with the Coven for a century and trusted none of them.
Tactical note: Her sisters' channel is her armour: break it, one bubble at a time. When she takes everyone's hair at once, run for the green circles.
The Grand Witch
The first demon, made from a human soul, and the last seal on Lucifer's cage. She makes deals she means to keep.
Tactical note: When she binds you with a contract, pay it in damage before the hounds come. Keep a headstone between you and her light.
Lilith
The Morningstar, the second archangel, cast down for refusing to bow. The order wrote that he must never walk free, and set down every way to keep him in.
Tactical note: He is proud: when he pauses to speak, he is open. Spend your strongest blows on his monologues.
Lucifer
The Devil as he is under the vessel: an archangel of light, free in his own Hell.
Tactical note: Six faces, six fights. The rings of the Horsemen that opened the way are his weakness: mind which phase you spend them in.
Lucifer, Uncaged
The Scribe of God, who wrote down every word and kept a few for himself.
Tactical note: Neither his hand nor his book can be hurt: dodge them and strike the scribe. Obey the Word, and it passes.
Metatron
The first archangel, the Sword of Heaven, God's most loyal son and his cruellest.
Tactical note: Never say yes. And watch the lance: when it is stuck in the floor, it can be taken.
Michael
An angel of Heaven's administration who reprogrammed her own kind. The order knew her only from what she did to the angels it questioned: they did not remember being questioned.
Tactical note: Cut down her guards first, and keep near the others: her chair's line finds whoever stands most alone. Strapped in, struggle.
Naomi
The Horseman of plague, who sows sickness and keeps it in vials.
Tactical note: Drink his antidotes and burn his flies; fire is the only thing they fear.
Pestilence
The archangel of healing, and of the storm. He means to finish the Apocalypse his brothers started.
Tactical note: Holy oil holds an archangel. Light a ring with him inside and the storm is yours for a moment.
Raphael

A witch of the Grand Coven, thrown out for being better than they were and saying so. The order filed her under 'tolerated, watched': she sold to hunters as readily as to anyone, and never once lost a client she meant to keep.
Tactical note: In her own house she does not fight fair. Kill her raven before it takes your hair; free her hexed, never kill them; and when she rises to recite, break every bowl.
Rowena MacLeod
The first of the Four Horsemen, who needs no army: he sets neighbours on each other and watches.
Tactical note: Raise your shield just before his blow lands: a parry stuns him and opens him wide.
War
A middle manager of Heaven, fond of paperwork and of other people's suffering. The order's file on him is mostly his own memoranda.
Tactical note: File his forms before you swing: an unfiled form leaves your blows worth a quarter. Later, read his docket; he tells you what comes next.
Zachariah

Built for the Men of Letters in the 1930s: concrete, steel and a warding laid into the walls themselves, so that nothing supernatural can find it or force its way in. It has its own power, its own water and enough books to last a lifetime.
Everything in it was left as it was in 1958: the typewriters, the lamps, the coffee cups. The order expected to come back.
The Bunker

The war room's table was more than a map. The order's engineers set a projector under its glass that drew the land from survey sheets and from the reports of every member in the field, and refreshed it as the reports came in.
Its blueprint was filed with the order's other inventions, in case a chapter house ever needed its own. The order fell before anyone built a second.
The Order's Cartography
The war room's map table was the order's great machine: reports of strange deaths from every corner of the country pinned where they happened, and lines drawn between them until a pattern showed.
A Man of Letters never went into a case blind. He read the file, he packed what the file told him to, and he wrote it up when he came home, so the next man would know a little more.
The Case Files

Most of the archive's vault held things: a ring that makes its wearer quick and hungry, a doll that cannot be burned, a mirror that shows the wrong room. Every one of them helps a little and costs a little.
Never use one you have not identified. The order catalogued what each one does before anyone was allowed to carry it.
Cursed Objects
The dungeon's floor is a single great trap, painted and sealed, with an iron chair bolted at its heart. The order questioned demons there, and never once let one go.
A trap holds what it was drawn to hold. Break one line, by scuff, crack or flood, and it holds nothing.
Devils' Traps
A sigil is a sentence in a language older than men. The order learned to change a word here and there: a little further, a little longer, a little cheaper, never stronger than the language allows.
Each formula they worked out has its own Latin name. Write it into your grimoire like any other sigil.
Formulae
A Legacy, son of a Legacy, initiated on the night the order fell. He escaped through time with the key and a box he would die for, carrying the Men of Letters into a world that had forgotten them.
He is a Winchester, and so, in his own careful way, a hunter's grandfather. He is also, as he will tell anyone who listens, not a hunter at all.
Henry Winchester

Founded in the days of King Solomon, the Men of Letters were never hunters themselves. They were the ones who understood: they catalogued every creature, every spell and every rite they could find, and handed what they learned to the hunters who would use it.

Each generation's members were Legacies, the knowledge passed from father to son. In 1958 the order was wiped out in a single night, and its bunker locked behind them. Henry's own key is the only one left.
The Order of the Men of Letters
The spell bowl is a cook's art. The order's notebooks are full of new mixtures: a different liquid, two more ingredients, a different form of words, and an old effect comes out of the smoke.
A rite you have researched is yours: pour, add, light and recite, as the page says.
Rites
They take a face by taking a skin, and shed it when they want another. Their eyes betray them on film: a flash of silver that no human eye throws back.
Silver hurts them; a silver blade to the heart kills them. Trust nobody you have not tested with silver.
On Shapeshifters

A key cut for one door only, and that door was built to keep out worse than burglars. The order hid it in a box warded against every creature they knew; Abaddon, a Knight of Hell, crossed half a century to take it.
Do not lose it. There is no locksmith on earth who could make another.
The Key
The Men of Letters' oldest enemies: occultists who gave their magic to a war, and then their souls to stay alive after it. Necromancers, every one, and very hard to keep dead.
The order's files on them are thick and incomplete. The last line in the last one, in Henry's hand: 'Burn the bodies.'
The Thule Society
Vampirism is a blood-borne infection. A nest has an alpha and a brood; most were people once, and some can still be cured with the blood of the one who turned them.
The order's rule: dead man's blood to stop it, a blade to the neck to end it. Burn the nest.
On Vampires
A curse of the blood, passed on with a bite. Most never know what they do at night until they wake in the woods with blood on their hands.
Silver to the heart, or silver anywhere it counts. The order kept a werewolf's silver bullets in the armoury, and a cage in the dungeon for the cases that came in early.
On Werewolves
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ascensio: The great enemies are not killed with the steel that kills a black-eyed demon. The longer the road, the more they can take: under two thousand points of health for the Yellow-Eyed Demon, seventy thousand for the Author. Each is measured against an Angel Blade ascended as far as the road has let you: a dozen or two good blows for the first, some sixty for the last. A sharper edge, the right bane, a crit or a rune shortens the fight; nothing lets you skip it, for no blow carries them past the next turn of the battle.

Ascension is how a weapon keeps up. At the Hellforge, put the weapon in its slot and an Ascension Shard in the slot at the far left, then Ascend. Each tier wants the shard of that tier and five levels for each: I, then II, up to V. The weapon's own damage, and everything it does when you hold use, is multiplied: x6 at I, x15 at II, x30 at III, x55 at IV and x90 at V. A small mark of gems on its icon shows how far it has come.
The first shard is made by a minor rite, by night, in a small circle: two demon blood, two hellfire embers, a salt and a quartz, lit with an amethyst shard that the rite consumes.

The others are left by the great enemies, one or two to every hunter who fought, every time they fall: Azazel and Lilith leave the second; Lucifer, the Trickster and the Horsemen War, Famine and Pestilence the third; the Broken Chorus, Metatron, Amara and Death the fourth; Lucifer Uncaged and Michael the fifth.

Spells and the powers of Heaven and Hell have nothing to ascend. Against a great enemy they grow with you instead, by the highest shard your victories have earned, or by the Ascension of the catalyst in your other hand if that is higher. Against anything else they stay as they are. Edge runes grow with the blade: each adds a tenth of its damage.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ash.0: The road door at the edge of your island leads to the heart of Heaven, where the souls' Heavens meet: Harvelle's Roadhouse, the way it was before it burned. Pool table, jukebox, the bar. Behind it, wiping a glass, is Ash: the mullet, the genius, the man who hacked Heaven's wiring and never left.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ash.1: Talk to him. He knows what is waiting for you next, more or less, and he keeps the list of Heavens that are open to visitors: hunters online who welcome guests, and the ones who trust you. Pick one and he sends you through. He can open or close your own Heaven to visitors too.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ash.2: The door at the back of the Roadhouse leads home to your own island.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.author_c: One cabin in the whole world, eight to twelve thousand blocks from where it all began, in a quiet wood or meadow. Logs, a porch with a rocking chair, a chimney, and a desk with a typewriter under the back window.

Before he expects you, it stands empty, but not silent: drafts thrown on the floor, empty bottles in the corners, and a page left in the typewriter. Read it. It is about you, and it stops exactly where you are.
He only comes home once "Find the Author" has been cast. After that, while anyone is near, he is at his desk.
The Cabin at the End of the World
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.azazel.0: The yellow-eyed one, and the first of the great ones you can reach. Call him up at night in a great circle: three demon blood, three sulfur, two salt, and fire.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.azazel.1: Samuel Colt's iron still holds him. Rails rise in a circle and pentagram around the altar, and he will not step inside while they are charged. Knock him in, shoot him in, or, once his vessel cracks, stand behind the rails when he rushes you as smoke: he goes in a straight line and does not swerve. Held in the rails, he is yours to hit while they go dark and charge again, one by one.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.azazel.2: Do not meet his eyes when they burn yellow. He throws what he tears out of the ground, drags you to him with a hand, brings the nursery fire down in lines along the floor. His smoke goes into the monsters around him and makes them his; where there are none, he calls demons up. Traps and salt do nothing to him.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.azazel.3: His blood forges the Key to the Cage. His death opens the way to Lilith.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.azazel.c: He leaves two vials of his blood, every time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.black_ey: The common kind, and the one you will meet first: a demon riding someone it took, out in the dark of the Overworld. It brawls up close, and every few seconds it flicks you away with a gesture.

Hurt one badly and it will try to flee its vessel as black smoke, taking its blood with it. Stand it on a devil's trap and it cannot leave; the Snare holds it for a breath.  Ruby's knife always draws blood. Holy water scalds them, Smite hits them twice as hard, and salt is a wall they will not cross.
Only a demon killed by a hunter leaves its blood. You will need a great deal of it.
A black-eyed demon, riding a stolen body
What they leave: blood, sulfur, now and then a page
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.blood_vi: A glass bottle used on another player draws a vial of their blood; it stings them a little. Sneak and use it in the air to cut your own palm instead, which stings more.
Poured into a bowl, the blood leads the Locating spell straight back to whoever it came from. Keep a vial of each person you hunt with. You will be glad of it the night one of them goes missing.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.book_giv: I gave Rowena the Book. She took it like a cat takes cream, and for a moment she almost looked grateful. She trusts me more now, which is to say a little.
The Grand Coven will not let her keep it. Ask her how to call them: she will tell you, and when their Grand Witch is dead she will take the Mark off you herself.
She is my ally now. She teaches me as before, and she keeps her bargains. Mostly.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.book_kep: I kept the Book. Rowena laughed, and it was not a nice laugh. She will not teach me or sell me anything again, and she greets me with nothing but threats.
She wants it back. Read the Book in her house at night and she will come for it: that is the fight, on her ground. Win, and the Grand Coven, who never forgave her, will owe me for it.
Lost the Book? Abaddon's copy comes back to whoever fights her again.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.book_of_: Bound in skin, written in blood: the darkest spells ever set down. Abaddon carried it; everyone who fought her gets their own copy, straight into the pack (or kept for them if they were away). Lose it and win it again by fighting her again.
Somewhere in it is the spell that undoes the Mark of Cain. Only a witch could read it, and I know one who would very much like to: see What to Do with the Book.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.borax.0: Plain laundry borax is the one thing in the world that burns a Leviathan. Grind two salt, sand and bone meal into a blend, and bake it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.borax.1: Rub a box straight into a Leviathan, or bottle it to throw: it bursts like a splash potion, burns every Leviathan it touches, sheds their disguises, finishes a severed head and dries their black goo.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.boss_dif: The world's difficulty decides how a great enemy fights, and the fight keeps the difficulty it began with: changing it halfway changes nothing.

On Easy they have three quarters of their health, hit for two thirds, warn longer, rest longer, leave you more time to punish them and bring half their servants. On Hard they have a third more health, hit a third harder, strike sooner and rest less, and call more help. Hardcore is harsher still.
Peaceful is the story: they still answer the summons, with half their health, a third of their bite, slow warnings and no servants at all.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.bound_bl: A vial of someone's blood, bound to them in the spell bowl: pour in their blood, add redstone and a string, and recite. An Infernal working. The vial remembers whose it is.
Lilith will not come for a sheet of paper any more: her contract is signed in bound blood. Keep the vials apart; the label is the only thing that tells two of them apart to anyone but the bowl.
Bound blood, and the vial it starts as
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.bowl_liq: Use a bottle on the bowl to pour it in: water, holy water, demon blood, honey, dragon's breath, a potion, or a vial of someone's blood. An empty bottle scoops a dose back out.
Use anything else on it to drop it in. Each spell's page lists exactly what it takes. Grave dirt, ectoplasm, bones and salt turn up in more than one of them, so keep some by.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.broken_c: A choir that sang before the Throne until the Throne was empty, and ran together into one broken thing. It is woken on the summit of a Hymnal Spire, in a thunderstorm: lay the Shattered Hymn on the Choir Altar and ring its three notes on the bells. The temple window on the stair shows them, left to right. A wrong note starts the hymn over.

Its faces sing, its wings beat, its wheels see. Break each in turn: bring the wings down to the stone, strike the eyes while they are open. Meet no open eye, or hide behind stone, and hide in a pillar's shadow from its light.
When it sings its Hymn, one bell lights: ring the bell it sings and it will kneel. Up there, a fall from the summit is forgiven, once.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cain.0: Nobody makes you fight him. If you do, it is at night in his yard, a ring sixteen blocks wide that his own hives stand just outside. Three phases, a third of his strength each.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cain.1: The Beekeeper: three lunges in a row, each down a red lane drawn just before it, and swarms of bees in yellow circles that sting, poison and blind.
