journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cain.2: The Mark awakens: a ploughing swing that tears up a red cone of earth; Abel's blood, a red ring of spikes round him with the green ground at his feet the only safe place; and farm tools hurled down violet lanes.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cain.3: The Father of Murder takes up the First Blade: a red circle where you stand, then he is behind you and the blade comes down; and the Mark's flare, which burns the whole yard but for three green shelters toward his hives. Run for them.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cain.4: His own First Blade bites him half as hard again. As he dies he kneels and offers the Mark to everyone who fought him. Refuse it and you may still take it later, at his grave in the plot under the oak.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cain.cap: What he leaves: his bust and three jars of honey (a bust and one jar in a rematch)
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cains_ad: Rowena wrote it down for me in her elegant hand: "Bees. End of the roads. Knock." The ink is witchcraft: use the note and it tells which way his farm lies and how far, and the needle drawn on it turns toward his gate.
Lose it and ask her again: she will write another, with a sigh.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cains_fa: A quiet farm, far out where the roads give up, between eighteen hundred and four thousand blocks from the world's heart: a fieldstone farmhouse, a red barn, four fields round a yard, a well, a row of hives on the east side and a fenced plot under an oak. The man who keeps it is Cain: the first murderer, the first Knight of Hell, retired.

He only comes out to hunters who have put Lucifer back in his box and have not yet beaten him. He tends his hives, and he will talk: who he is, a jar of honey once a day, and the Mark, which he will not hand over.
Push him and he will test you, but only at night, in his own yard. Nobody makes you do it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cains_ho: A jar from the east hives. Cain gives one a day to whoever asks him nicely, and leaves three when he falls the first time (one in a rematch).
It is food like any honey. To someone who bears the Mark of Cain it is more: a spoonful quiets a quarter of the Mark's Thirst. That is how he kept his own Mark asleep for a century: bees, and this.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.call_the: Rowena told me how, once I had given her the Book. A great circle by night in the Overworld; bound blood, hexed ink, two amethyst shards, a ghast tear, a candle and two nether warts on the altar; her calling card to wake it (it is not spent); a hundred and twenty mana.
Only someone who gave her the Book can do it. The fight opens round the altar, eighteen blocks wide.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cases.0: Ask Henry in the war room and he hands you a case: a file and a map to a place a few hundred blocks away where something has been killing. Read the file (use it): the place, the suspect, what else is known.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cases.1: Go there and finish what you find. A solved case pays in field notes (filed in your Archive) and sometimes a cursed artifact, and writing it up at a desk is research of its own. Let it go cold and Henry will find you another.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.catalyst: The ember staff, from sticks, sulfur and flint in a small circle. Opposite a grimoire, your hellfire burns hotter and bolts burst where they land. Alone, it hurls fireballs.
The Enochian orb: spells cost less and come back faster, and bolts split in three. Alone, it throws a seeking glyph.

The censer of grace, holy: holy spells strike harder, Burst lingers and Ward grows. Alone, hold use for a beam of light that lights the ground where it falls. Against the Darkness, that beam is worth more than any blade.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_an: Two forms of the second tier, both shelved in the bunker library.

Chain throws a bolt of force at the first thing in your line, up to ten blocks, then leaps on to up to three more, each the nearest not yet struck within five blocks of the last and each a fifth weaker than the one before. A harmful spell leaps between foes, a helpful one between friends.

Glyph plants a small sigil on the floor where you look (within six blocks; at your feet if you look at nothing). It lies quiet for thirty seconds until something hostile to you steps on it; then the spell goes off on everything standing on it, and the glyph is spent. You can keep three down at once: a fourth wipes out your oldest.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_au: Sworn hunters may walk through their own garrison. In the throne room, ask the Lord for an audience: a task, a promotion, or, if you are a Commander, a challenge for the throne. A task allows 5 days to slay a named officer of the other side, win a skirmish, or bring tribute. The throne has little patience for unfinished work.

The book carries up to 3 messages a day, one per officer, with replies at dawn. Ask for a pact, aid or sponsorship, send an insult, or deliver a Lord's orders. Distance keeps the blade away for a while; it does not soften the answer.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_bo: Officers keep a measure of regard for one another and for you, from −100 to 100. At −40 you are a rival; at −70, a grudge. A grudge can become a challenge or a betrayal. At 50, regard becomes loyalty. The book shows which bonds have taken root.

A stolen promotion, a lost feud or a betrayal sours regard; help and pacts warm it. Left alone, it fades day by day. A pact lasts days and prevents challenges between the two who swore it. An oath buys time, never eternity.

At a ritual altar, offer a book with the Leviathan officer's name written inside and a flask of borax. The rite calls that officer into the ring. Write the name exactly: the Board does not answer vague complaints.
A Leviathan challenge is always to the death. There is no surrender to negotiate and no rank for a hunter to inherit. Bring enough borax to make the ending permanent.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_ch: At a ritual altar, offer a book with the officer's name written inside and cast down a Gauntlet of Ash for a demon or fallen officer, or a Seal of Summons for an angel. A name written carelessly calls nobody; a name written correctly calls trouble.

The officer comes alone within 30 seconds, to a ring around the altar. There is no escort to cut through and no excuse to step outside. Challenge a superior of your own side and the duel is for that officer's post.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_du: A duel is fought inside a ring of 8 blocks. Escorts stand aside; step out and you forfeit. Two of one side fight until one yields, below 10% health. Across the sides, the duel is to the death: a proper kill, with a 1.5× reward. Keep your feet where your courage is.

An officer with a grudge may call you out after an improper killing, a flight or a humiliation. You have 2 days of play to answer; time away does not count. Refuse or let it lapse, and the chain calls it cowardice: the officer gains a level and you lose a rank if you hold a post. At most one challenge waits on you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_fe: The officers of a chain are always at each other's throats. Every few days two of them fight it out: an underling against its master, or two rivals of one rank. Win against a master and you take its rank; any other win is worth a level. The loser leaves with a scar, and one feud in four ends in a death, for a while.

Come upon a feud, near the territory of either of them, and you will see it: both officers and their escorts tearing into each other. Wait for the winner, or step in; if you kill one, the feud is the other's.

When a Lord dies the throne is not filled at once. For three to five days it stands empty, the chain's feuds flare up every day, and the Commanders fight over it. The one with the most wins is crowned.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_le: A third chain has convened at SucroCorp. These are the Old Ones out of Purgatory, wearing human skins. The Board answers to neither Heaven nor Hell: humans, demons and angels are all food. Every hunter is an enemy. There is no parley, no sponsorship and no place for you in its ranks.

Their ranks wear corporate titles: Associate, Manager, Director, Vice President and Chairman. Behind the smiles are the same promotions, rivalries and vacant posts as any chain, with an appetite that never clocks off.

An officer only stays dead when borax finishes it. Bagging its severed head or carrying it away may end the encounter, but the chain counts it as a botched kill. The officer may return, scarred and hungry. Finish the job with borax.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_of: Hell and Heaven both keep ranks, and the rank and file are not as faceless as they look. A black-eyed demon or an angel that kills a hunter earns a name and a place in its side's chain: Soldier, Captain, Lieutenant, Commander and, over them all, a single Lord. Each chain holds at most ten Soldiers, six Captains, three Lieutenants, two Commanders and one Lord. Its officers are the same creatures as ever, only stronger with every rank and every kill, quicker with their powers, and never alone above the lowest rank.
The Pit's chain stirs once Azazel has fallen; the Host's once the angels walk the Earth, and its angels only Fall after Metatron. Each wakes with a Lord and a staff already in place.

Kill a hunter, and an officer may rise. Its side marks the hunter, and from then on officers come looking for them, more often the more they have lost to that chain. Angels and demons who serve the same side are never hunted by its chain.

Kill an officer, and its post falls vacant; it is filled again a day or two later. The one above it will come for you within a few days. Strike it down with the wrong weapon and it may return, scarred, a few days later; a demon only stays dead to demon-bane or holy smiting, an angel only to an angelic blade. Slay a Lord and its throne stands empty for days while its Commanders feud over it.

Every day the chains move on their own. Underlings challenge their masters, empty posts are filled, officers turn on their masters, angels Fall, and the two chains skirmish with each other. The Chain of Command tab of this book keeps both chains and their history.

Every officer can be found. The Lord and its Commanders hold court in a stronghold far from the world's centre: the Pit Castle and the Monastery. Soldiers roam territories near the centre, where hunters live; Captains roam further out, toward their stronghold, and Lieutenants on its marches; come close and the officer shows itself, escort and all. A promotion moves it. Choose an officer in this book to read roughly where it roams and where it was last seen; a Men of Letters war table marks every territory exactly, and the chosen one's last sighting.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_pa: Any hunter may crouch and speak to an officer of the other side. Temperament decides whether it listens: Cunning officers almost always hear an offer; Cruel ones never do. Lowering yourself is a request for a hearing, not a promise of safety.

Tribute may buy a truce: the officer leaves you alone for one day. Demons may also take a bribe for a rival's whereabouts, or a deal: kill the rival for three days of peace. Break your word and the demon remembers. Loyal angels do not sell rivals or make those deals.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_st: Each chain's Lord keeps a stronghold, thousands of blocks from the world's centre and on opposite sides of it. The Pit's is a castle of blackstone ringed by fire, with cages, chains and rooms nobody should see. The Host's is a white monastery, a cloister and a bell tower, quiet as a held breath. A Men of Letters war table marks both.

Past the gate, rooms of guards with no names, the Pit's or the Host's rank and file; at the far end, the throne room, where the Lord sits with its Commanders and no one else. Below it, a vault. The guards you kill stay dead until a new Lord takes the throne; while the throne stands empty, half the garrison is gone.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_sw: A sworn angel or demon can hold a real post. Faction rank I means Soldier, II Captain, III Lieutenant and IV Commander. The throne comes only by defeating the Lord in a duel. A hunter who becomes Lord holds the title, not the stronghold; stone does not swear allegiance as easily as flesh.

To enter, find a sponsor: an officer with at least 60 regard who will speak for you, or ask the Lord at an audience. Rise through a sponsor, through the Lord's tasks with at least 50 regard and a free post, or through a duel. Ambitious officers can challenge you in turn. A rank is a place to defend.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_te: Every named officer has one of six temperaments: Ambitious, Loyal, Cruel, Cunning, Proud or Zealous. It colours what you hear and whom the officer clashes with; it never changes how hard a blow lands. Read the person before you draw the blade.

There is a past behind the title. Demons remember the rack and the bodies they stole; angels remember a choir, a willing vessel and the service that earned a post. The fallen remember why they lost Heaven. Choose an officer in the book to read what remains of that story.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chain_wa: The officers' country, from 300–2900 blocks out, is divided into 24 sectors of 15°. Each side begins with the half facing its stronghold. Skirmishes and duels across the sides push a sector until it changes hands; the officers there fall back. The front is a border you can move with a blade.

When a hunter is near, skirmishes are fought in the world. Help a side and earn its regard. A Lord wronged by a killing may swear a vow and name a champion, with a duel due within 3 days. A grievance at the throne can put a blade in the field.

Every 14 days or so, war may be declared for 3–5 days. Skirmishes break out three times as often. The side ahead at the end takes a sector and its Lord gains a level; the losing chain is shaken for 2 days. Count the victories, not the speeches.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chairman: The first Lord waits at the head of his boardroom table in the penthouse of SucroCorp. The door opens only to the anointed Righteous Bone; an ordinary bone is no invitation. Prepare before you walk into the meeting.

If the founder falls, the Board falls with him: no interregnum, no successor, no new hires. Its ground is divided among the other chains, and whoever is left holds out in the tower until they are hunted down. Only then can the rite of summoning call the founder back for a rematch.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.choir_ec: One small voice of the Broken Chorus, a wheel around a single eye, set loose every time one of its faces breaks. It circles the choir and sings.

While an echo lives, the Chorus winds up faster and its Hymn cuts deeper, and now and then the echo sings a sharp note at whoever is closest. Kill them as they come. The Colt takes one with a single round.
A Choir Echo: one small voice
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chrism.0: Holy oil, blessed in the spell bowl: two doses of holy water, a holy oil and a glistering melon slice. An Enochian working, and an easy one.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chrism.1: It is not thrown and not burned: rites ask for it as a reagent. The angel blade takes one chrism and one holy water where it used to take two holy water, and Metatron will not come down without it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chuck.0: Every story has someone who wrote it. With the Cage shut for good, the Fallen Star still burns: it remembers who lit it. Somewhere very far from here there is a cabin, and a man at a typewriter.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chuck.1: He calls himself Chuck. He is pleasant, a little shabby, fond of whiskey and of the sound of his own prose. He is also the one who wrote the salt, the sigils, Hell and every great enemy you have faced. Nothing you do surprises him, and he is careful to let you know it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chuck.2: He will talk for as long as you like. When you tell him you are ready, he stands up, straightens his clothes, and the cabin is unwritten around you. What follows is his test, in five chapters. It is long: bring friends, your best gear, and patience. He cannot be hurt by anything but the story breaking.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.chuck_ch: Each chapter is a phase, and each has an arena of its own: the old one dissolves into letters while the new one rises block by block. The chapter's title is written across your sight as it begins.
I. Eden. A golden garden; he fights as a man, in a flannel shirt, and can be hurt like one. II. Hell and the Cage. A light suit, the old stone of the Pit. Still a man, still mortal enough.

III. The Chorus's Storm. Here he stops pretending: a figure of white light fourteen blocks tall, four rings of sacred geometry, a halo of keys, two giant hands. Nothing touches him until you tear the manuscript pages that float around him; each torn page opens a short window.

IV. The Scribe's Library. His four rings carry weak points. Break every point of one ring and he is open for a few seconds; break all four rings and his core lies bare for longer. Don't trust the credits if they roll.

V. The Blank Page. The arena erases itself while you fight. He narrates what you will do next - runs, stands still, looks away, jumps, kneels - and the only way to hurt him is to do the opposite. Every contradiction cracks him.

Throughout: his Snap erases a marked frame after a countdown (leave it, or break his line of sight); keys rain and lines of text sweep the floor; Backspace drags you back to where you stood moments ago; and he rewrites the rules - gravity, water that burns, light that hurts, a floor of lava. In the divine chapters the old enemies come back in ink, each for one famous blow.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.cleansin: Purification cleanses everyone near the bowl, and always the one who cast it: possession, jinxes, bleeding and marks lift, minds steady, the possessed are themselves again, curse bags burn and ghosts scatter. A variant of it breaks a crossroads deal.
Binding holds the nearest creature to the bowl, a ghost before anything else, never a player or one of the great ones. It cannot stray more than a few steps for as long as the bowl stands.
Banishing is the big hammer. Every ghost near the bowl is laid to rest for good, and demons and hellhounds are cast back into the dark, leaving nothing behind.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.clerk_an: Heaven's office staff, in shirtsleeves, vests and green visors. Zachariah calls three at a time. Each carries a rubber stamp: a clerk's stamp says DENIED just as his does, and your wounds stop closing for a while.
Cut one down and it may drop its Approval Stamp. Use it on your form and the form is filed on the spot, wherever you stand.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.concealm: Concealment hides you for three minutes from demons, angels, spirits and hellhounds: they neither see nor hunt you. Never from the great ones, and never from a hound that has come to collect on your debt. Strike one of them and it is broken.
Second Sight is the other way round. For three minutes you see what hides: ghosts, hellhounds, invisible things and hidden curse bags, all outlined.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.consecra: Set a ritual altar where an abandoned church's broken altar stands and chalk a small circle round it. Chrism, two holy waters and three white candles on the altar, flint and steel to light it, forty-five mana.

It only takes on a real church's ground, and only once per church. It blesses sixteen blocks round the altar as holy ground and makes the church a sanctuary: every second, any demon or spirit inside is driven out to its edge. The great ones are not bound by it.
The first time a church is cleansed it leaves something on the altar: an Enochian sigil page, of the third tier at most.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.corrupti: A demon's powers burn Corruption, and it seeps back on its own: an empty vessel is full again in five minutes, whatever your rank. Standing in fire or lava doubles that; crouch and keep still in the Nether or in Hell and it comes three times as fast; crouch in the flames themselves, fire, soul fire or lava, and you are full in half a minute. Nothing comes back in the Mark of Cain's bloodlust, or in the Darkness's eclipse.

Harm done gives it too. Slay angels and rival hunters, and strike pacts: crouch and offer a villager an emerald, and they give you something for it (a fifth of your vessel), once each. Villagers who see your eyes run.

What hurts a demon still hurts you: salt lines stop you, a devil's trap holds you, holy water burns, and an exorcism tears the smoke out of you (it does not kill, but it leaves you empty). Demons and hellhounds of your own side leave you alone; the Host and angels hunt you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.coven_st: The Grand Witch's own staff, left to whoever beats her the first time: a tier IV Witchcraft catalyst. Held opposite a grimoire, Witchcraft sigils cost a fifth less and strike a quarter harder.

Its own spell is the Coven's hex: the foe it points at, up to eighteen blocks away, takes nine (more as the staff ascends) and, unless it is a great enemy or a player, eight seconds of the Curse of Frailty. Ten mana.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.coven_wi: The elite of a coven: forty-eight health, light armour, stronger magic, and a violet bubble that swallows the first fourteen points of harm you do her. A salt round or Break Hex shatters it at once, and the Colt goes straight through. Twenty seconds later it rises again.

Her worst trick is a curse. A violet circle opens under your feet: step out of it before she finishes, a little over a second, or you carry frailty or silence for thirty seconds. Silenced, you cast nothing.
If her familiar is gone she calls another, a cat or a raven, out of the smoke. She blinks away in smoke more often than her sisters do.
Some of them carry an embossed card in green ink. Read the page on Rowena's calling card before you throw it away.
A coven witch behind her bubble
A quarter of them leave their blood; a third carry a calling card
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.crossroa: Call the crossroads demon at night with the bowl: demon blood, a bone, grave dirt, an oxeye daisy and a damned contract. It steps out of the smoke beside the bowl, ready to deal. The old way works too: a box buried at night at a natural crossroads calls a wilder one (The Wild Crossroads, in this book).
It waits on you a couple of minutes, never attacking. Use it to hear the offer. Hit it, walk off, or take too long, and it leaves in smoke.
Name your wish and seal it with a kiss. Then the clock starts. One soul, one deal: you cannot owe twice.
A crossroads demon: sharp suit, red eyes
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.death.0: Older than God, thin, in a black suit, with a cane, and fond of junk food. Offer him the rings of War, Famine and Pestilence, with void essence and abyssal shards, and wake the circle with the Soul Scythe. Win or lose, he gives the three rings back.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.death.1: Your clock starts the moment he arrives. Hit him to wind it back. He fights with cane and scythe, reaping in arcs and throwing crescents; then his reapers come, whom you only see when your time is nearly up.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.death.2: Then the world of the dead takes the arena: everything turns grey, clocks run twice as fast, he steps through shadows and the reapers are always there. The world goes back and forth between the living and the dead. At the end he rides his pale horse: the end is the end.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.decapita: A sword or an axe through the neck of a Leviathan at half its health or less takes the head off. The body drops and lies helpless; the head crawls back to it on its tongue, and if they meet the Leviathan gets up again at half its health.

Blows do not hurt the head; they only knock it away. Keep it more than twelve blocks from its body for five seconds, bag it with an empty hand, burn it or throw borax on it, and the Leviathan is done for. A body left without its head for a minute dies anyway.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.demon_bl: Demon blood is the currency of everything that follows: blood chalk, devil's traps, Ruby's knife, every summoning. Only a demon a hunter kills leaves it, and only if it does not smoke out first.
Sulfur they drop freely, and it shows in Nether rock as ore. It feeds the Hellfire sigil and Enochian ink. Hellfire embers come only from exorcism: a demon cast back down leaves one where it stood.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.demon_br: A demon that picked the biggest body it could find and then made it bigger. It lumbers until it has room, then it charges; get close and it brings both fists down on the ground around it. Keep moving and keep your distance.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
A possessed brute, chains round its fist
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.demon_cu: A demon can be made human again, a night at a time. Mix purified blood at the bowl (a vial of blood in holy water), then stand inside a devil's trap and give it, with holy water, at the altar: three times, on three different nights. The last night gives back the hearts the crossroads took. You lose your ranks, and must wait three days before you may choose a side again.
The cure, one night of three
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.demon_fl: It folds into black smoke and comes out behind you, and its first cut out of the smoke lands twice. When it vanishes, turn around.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.demon_oc: A robed demon who keeps its distance and hurls hellfire. Rarer than the black-eyed kind, and smarter about it. Close the gap, or break its line of sight and make it come to you.

Occultists are where the pages come from. They carry torn sigil pages and bowl spell pages far more often than the brawlers do, and more sulfur. In Hell some of them carry one of Crowley's damned contracts.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.demon_pa: Crossroads Demon. At the crossroads, tick "Bind my soul" before you seal a deal: if the hounds come for you and take you, you rise a demon instead of losing what you were owed. Or wish to be made one of them and become one at once, for two hearts the demon keeps until you are cured. Smoke rushes you where you look, fire cannot burn you, a hellhound comes when you call, black eyes see in the dark, and you can close a throat from afar.

Prince of Hell. By night in the Overworld: Azazel's blood, a choir shard and two demon bloods. You no longer hunger nor sleep; you can seize what you look at and hurl it, or ride a mob for twenty seconds. Your eyes turn yellow, and a ring of hellfire bursts out of you at will.

Knight of Hell. Only a Prince who already bears the Mark of Cain (taken from Cain himself) may rise: the Angel Tablet and two demon bloods, with the First Blade to raise it. The Blade answers its Knight and every kill heals you, but the Mark thirsts: go too long without a kill and its bloodlust drinks your Corruption, then your blood (read the page on the Mark). A wave of flame rolls out ahead of you, and you can step out of the shadow behind a foe, whose next wound cuts deeper.

King of Hell. Usurp the throne on the dais of Lucifer's Cage with a Fallen Star and Michael's Grace. Demons and hellhounds obey you, and from the throne every mob near you kneels. You wear the crown and the cloak. The Maw of Hell opens where you look and drags in all near it, and you can descend to Hell with the friends who kneel beside you. Hell is your realm: the same way takes you all back up to where you sleep.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.demon_to: The Pit's jailer. It throws a meat hook on a chain, drags you to it and holds you there while its friends go to work. Break line of sight before it throws.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.devils_t: A devil's trap is painted, not built. A square of chalk with a lit candle at each corner, demon blood, salt, paper and red dye on the altar: two traps. Use one on the floor and it paints the whole 3x3 seal around where you clicked, or nothing at all if it does not fit.

Any demon standing on any part of it is held fast. It can still turn and swing at you, but it cannot walk, jump or smoke out of its vessel. That last part is the point: a demon you trap is a demon you get to finish, and its blood with it.
The big ones laugh at paint. Azazel walks right over a trap and burns it on the way.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.dick_rom: The head of the Leviathans wears a good suit and a better smile. He is called in the Overworld once Raphael has fallen, with the anointed bone to wake a great circle; the bone comes back if you lose. Optional: nothing else needs him.

The Executive: a red ring round him throws everyone out of it; violet lanes are a contract, and whoever stands in one when he signs is bound; now and then his staff walk in, and they are not villagers.
The Maw: his head splits. A red cone is a bite; a red lane, a lunge that swallows the first hunter in it and spits them back out; red circles, black goo that stays and burns.
The Copy: he takes a hunter's face and hides among doubles in it. Hidden he takes almost nothing. Borax shows him: the doubles burst and he staggers, every blow landing harder.
The Flood: the boardroom drowns in goo that slows and burns. Borax dries islands in it, until a yellow ring warns that the goo is rolling back. Tentacles rise behind you down red lanes.
Dick Roman, head of Roman Enterprises
What he leaves: a shard of the Leviathan Tablet and his own borax sprayer the first time; borax after
A great rite can put out the sun. A great circle in the Overworld, by day: two crying obsidian, two black dye, an eye of ender, two demon blood and a sculk catalyst. It costs more mana than a hunter is born with.
For ten minutes the whole world goes dark. Demons walk by day, and more of them. The dead do not burn in the light that is left. Holy strikes bite a little deeper.
Only under an eclipse can the Darkness be called. That is the real reason you would ever do this.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.exorcism: Trap them first. Then a blood circle, two salt and a holy water on the altar, and fire. Every trapped demon within six blocks is cast out of its vessel and sent back down, and each one leaves a hellfire ember behind.

Embers are what the serious rites are paid in: the angel blade, the Hellforge, the Key itself. Every demon you kill in a trap instead of casting out is one ember you will not have. The Exorcise sigil does the same work, one trapped demon at a time.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.fallen_a: When Metatron was beaten, Heaven was emptied. Every angel in it fell that night, a sky full of burning stars. The ones that lived through the landing walk the earth now in torn clothes, their wings broken and burnt, and they can't fly any more. So they run, and they leap.
They blame us. Hunters and Heaven's sworn alike, they go for on sight; they fight the angels who did not fall. Hell's sworn they leave alone, mostly.
Same rule as any angel: an angel blade, or a very long night.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.familiar: A cat that sits too still, a raven that never flies far: a witch's eyes. A familiar that sees you within sixteen blocks marks you. You glow for three seconds, you feel watched, and every witch nearby turns on you, even the ones who cannot see you.

It steals, too. When it can, about once a minute, it runs at the nearest hunter, snips a lock of hair and bolts back to its witch, who curses you with it from afar until it is taken back. Kill the familiar and the lock drops where it dies.
While it lives within thirty-two blocks of her, its witch's magic is a quarter stronger. A familiar whose witch is dead goes wild after half a minute. Kill it first.

Rowena's working. Name a cat or a parrot you have tamed, with a taglock of its fur or feathers, within sixty-four blocks of the bowl: it becomes your familiar, healed and steadied a while (Regeneration and Resistance for a minute).
A familiar answers to Trace the Familiar. What else it can do for a witch is still being written.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.family_b: Saving people, hunting things. If you are reading this, you already know the world is not what they told you. Demons walk at night wearing people. The dead do not always stay down. And somewhere under it all, something is waiting in a Cage.
This journal is everything I know. Pages fill in as you see things, kill things and get your hands on things: a page you have not earned stays blank. Read in order if you are new. Start with salt.
Chalk comes from calcite and bone meal, and you will draw every circle in this book with it. Mix four chalk with a demon's blood and you have blood chalk, for the circles that matter.
The first tools of the trade
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.famine.0: A frail old man in a wheelchair, and he is always hungry. Call him with rotten flesh, bread, wheat and salt, lit with flint and steel, once Lucifer has fallen. His ground is dead farmland and rotten crops.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.famine.1: Near him your hunger drains away, and whatever you eat close to him feeds him instead. Then he stands up, and his starving thralls shuffle in to be eaten: if one reaches him he drinks its soul and heals, and he feeds on anything living nearby too. Kill them on the way.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.famine.2: On his black horse he feeds on you: he lifts a hunter and drains health and hunger. Everyone else, hit him hard to make him let go. Alone, hold on: he drops you when there is little left.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.find_the: The page for this spell is never found by chance. It falls at your feet the moment you have beaten every great enemy before him: Azazel, Lilith, Lucifer, the Broken Chorus, Metatron, the Darkness and Lucifer Uncaged.
Cast in the Overworld, the smoke draws a map with his mark on it: the Author's Address. From then on, he waits for you at home.
Fallen Star, ink, paper, holy water
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.fly_swar: Pestilence's flies, a buzzing cloud that chases you, blinds you and leaves you sick. Steel goes straight through them; only fire takes them.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.four_hor: To open the Cage itself, down in Hell, the Key is not enough. It wants the rings of the four Horsemen, and there is only one way to get a Horseman's ring: win it from him. Once Lucifer has fallen they will answer a call.
War, Famine and Pestilence come up here in the world, each to his own rite, in any order. Death comes too, but only for a hunter who offers him the other three rings. He gives them back, win or lose.
Each one lays his own ground over the arena and rides his horse for the last part of the fight. Beat him and he leaves his ring, his likeness and his horse, every time you beat him.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.four_sch: Every effect sigil, every bowl spell and every rite belongs to one of four schools. The school is the colour its light burns in, the mastery it trains and the discount it earns. A spell takes the school of its first effect; forms and modifiers belong to none, and are drawn in plain chalk white.
Enochian is Heaven's tongue, gold with a white heart: Smite, Mend, Banishing, and the Ward, the one form that is Heaven's own. Holy water and consecrations are Enochian rites.
Infernal is Hell's craft, red fire with orange embers: Hellfire, and the summonings and pacts that call on the pit.
Witchcraft is the old art, magenta smoke on plum: Frost among the sigils, and most of what the spell bowl does, from hex bags to locating spells.
Hunter is the plain lore of salt, silver and iron, steel grey with a blue edge: Repel, Reveal, Exorcise and the Snare, and the rites that drive things out.
Infernal: fire red and ember orange
A pagan god of mischief, they say, who plays deadly pranks on the people who deserve them. He is not. He is Gabriel, the archangel who ran away from his brothers' war and hid in plain sight. Bait him by night with sweets inside a ring of holy oil, and he drags you into TV Land.

Lay two holy oils, a cake and two sugar in a small circle in the Overworld, by night, and wake it with the Trickster's Bait; the bait is eaten every time. He steps out of the fire laughing, and the world round the altar turns into a television studio. Nobody else's road needs him: he is a side show, for the fun of it.

He fights through four channels, a quarter of his strength each, and changes channel when you take it: static, a new set built round you, a new costume. In the sitcom, the game show and the hospital he plays by the show's rules, and so must you. In the commercial, five of him stand at five podiums, and only one is real.

He is not a fair fighter, but he plays fair by his own rules: learn each channel's and he is not as strong as he looks. (TV Land, in this book, tells them channel by channel.) Win, and he leaves his toys.
He can be baited again, as often as you like, one bait each time: then he leaves his trophy and some candy, and now and then his remote or his blade.
What he leaves the first time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.gabriel_: An archangel blade with a golden edge, and his sense of humour: now and then a strike calls up two fleeting doubles of you, who strike the same foe a little more before they wink out.

Gabriel's oldest trick: more of himself. His doubles wear what he wears and grin the way he grins, but one blow and they are gone. In the sitcom they come through the doors as extras; in the hospital they are nurses in white caps, walking to him to patch him up; in the commercial they are the spokesmen at the podiums. A Reveal sigil dissolves one on the spot.
One of him. Or is it?
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.garrison: Soldiers of Heaven loyal to Raphael, in storm grey and silver, their wings folded. When he is hurt he calls four of them, and each one holds a thread of grace to him while it lives: a ribbon of warm light, and every thread heals him a little every second.

A thread breaks while someone stands in it, and for good when its angel dies. They are only soldiers: a few good blows bring one down. Watch for him laying his hands on a fallen one: he raises one of them, once.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.general_: Michael's own armour, white and gold and written over in Enochian. He leaves one piece each time he falls, one you do not have yet. Worn whole, it wards off holy harm and raises a wing of light that takes a blow for you every thirty seconds.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ghosts.0: Old graves hold more than bones. At night a ghost rises near them and haunts whoever comes close: the cold bites and slows you, the lights die, things fly. You will see it only in flickers, and when it lashes out.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ghosts.1: Ordinary harm goes straight through it. Cold iron, holy water or anything holy scatters it for a while, and now and then it leaves ectoplasm behind. Salt is a line it cannot cross, walls or no walls. Second Sight and the Reveal sigil show it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ghosts.2: It cannot be killed. It stays near its bones and sinks back into its grave at dawn. To be rid of it, see to the bones.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grace.0: An angel's powers burn Grace, and it comes back on its own: an empty vessel is full again in five minutes, whatever your rank. Standing on consecrated ground doubles that. Pray (crouch and keep still) and it comes three times as fast anywhere; pray on consecrated ground and you are full in half a minute. Consecrated ground is the ground around a ritual altar, a choir altar or an Enochian pillar, or any ground the consecration rite has blessed.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grace.1: Slaying demons gives Grace too (about a twelfth of your vessel each; a demon boss half of it). In the Darkness's eclipse nothing comes back, and she drinks what you have.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grace.2: What hurts an angel: holy oil set alight (it cannot cross the ring), the Enochian banishing sigil, an angel blade or Ruby's knife in another's hand (three times the harm), and the Darkness, who drinks Grace in her eclipse. Ghosts will not touch you, and the Host of Heaven does not see you as an enemy.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grand_wi: Only for the one who gave Rowena the Book: the Coven's rite calls her, wherever it is done, and she steps out of the smoke a few blocks from the altar with three sisters round her. Three phases, a third of her strength each.

The Coven's Shield: three coven witches channel into her from seven blocks away, and while even one still channels, every blow on her is swallowed. Break a channeler's own bubble (blows, a salt round, Break Hex) and she stops for twelve seconds; kill her and she is gone for good. Then the shield falls.
The Matriarch's Hexes: a blue circle under every hunter and then frost; an inferno, a red circle six blocks round her; and a violet circle that crushes and pins whoever is still in it.

The Mass Taglock: she holds a lock of everyone's hair. A red circle follows each hunter for two seconds, stops, and then the curse lands, twenty and frailty, on everyone not standing in one of the two green circles Rowena draws. Rowena arrives for this part: she cannot be hurt, and she throws bolts at the coven. Yellow smoke where the Grand Witch is about to land.
The Grand Witch of the Grand Coven
What she leaves: the Coven Staff and her bust the first time (a bust in a rematch)

Rowena's death pleased the Grand Coven. When she falls to someone who kept the Book, the Grand Witch walks out of the smoke on the battlefield. She cannot be harmed, and to anyone else she has nothing to say.
To you she owes one thing: the Mark taken off. She reads the cure from the Book, so you must carry it (she does not keep it), and she wants a vial of your own bound blood.
She leaves after two minutes with nobody near. Read the Book in Rowena's house again and she comes back.
The Grand Witch, owing a debt
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.great_fi: The great ones do not wander. You call them, by rite or by song, and they come with their own ground: a dome closes over the place and there is no leaving it until one of you is done. Only one such fight can hold a world at a time.

Every attack they have is written on the ground before it lands. Learn the colours: red is fire, blue is frost, violet is the mind's reach, gold is judgement, green is the one safe place. Move when you see them, and hit hardest while they recover.
Their ground breaks under them, and puts itself back together once it is over. If everyone falls or runs, they simply leave. Everyone who fought shares the credit for a kill.
The Watchers were sent to look after us, and some of them got hungry. A Grigori fades from sight and feeds on the soul of whatever it grabs, healing as it drinks. It serves the fallen.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.grimoire: A book, a vial of Enochian ink, chalk and leather. Ink is an ink sac, sulfur and salt in a glass bottle; you will want plenty of it.
The first time you open it its first pages make sense: Touch, Bolt, Smite and Mend. Everything else you learn from torn sigil pages.

It holds six pages, each a spell. Use it to cast the open page; sneak and turn the scroll wheel (or press the page key) to turn pages. Sneak-use opens this book, and the Scriptorium inside it is where spells are written: each page you inscribe costs a vial of ink.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.guild_di: Your guild keeps its own stance toward every faction: hostile, neutral or allied. A new guild is hostile to the Pit and the Host, and neutral to other guilds. SucroCorp is always hostile; there is no bargain with the Board.

Declare hostility on your own authority; peace requires both sides. Send and answer offers from the book. Allies never wage war against one another. Wild demons and angels judge a guild member by the stance of that guild, even when the hunter once served another side.
The front is divided into 24 sectors of 15°. A guild can hold ground there like the older factions, but needs its standard to keep a home. See The Standard before leaving your seat undefended.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.guild_fo: What you need: to have seen Lucifer fall, no place in another guild, 60 mana and one of the world's four guild places still free. Human, demon or angel, it makes no difference. Then go step by step.

1. The banner. Dye a banner the colour your guild will wear: its base colour becomes the guild's colour, patterns are not kept. Rename it on an anvil with the guild's name, 3 to 24 letters, digits, spaces or the marks ' - . &. No two guilds may share a name.

2. The circle. Set down a ritual altar and draw the small circle around it: eight chalk lines. Lay the offerings on the altar one at a time: two blocks of gold, two diamonds, salt, and a book for the charter, blank or written.

3. The rite. Light it with the renamed banner itself. The banner burns into a Guild Standard that carries the name and the colour. The rite refuses a banner never named on an anvil, and a hunter who already serves a guild.

4. The seat. Carry the standard into the Overworld, at least 300 blocks from the world's centre and 256 from any other seat (the Pit Castle, the Monastery, SucroCorp Tower or another guild's standard), and plant it. That founds the guild: you sit on its throne as its Lord, it takes its share of the front, and any post you held in the Pit or the Host is left behind.

5. First orders. Open the Chain of Command tab: your guild has its own record there. Choose an emblem, invite your first hunters and decide how you stand with the world. A new guild starts hostile to the Pit and the Host, neutral to the other guilds, and hostile to SucroCorp for good.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.guild_in: If the founder leaves or is away for thirty days, the throne stands empty. An interregnum lasts three days. The hunters of the guild may claim the throne from the book; hired NPCs cannot claim it.

Rival claimants fight each other for the succession. The victor takes the throne and the guild continues under its new Lord. If nobody claims it, the guild dissolves. A planted standard cannot save a guild that has nobody willing to lead it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.guild_le: Your guild's record in the Chain of Command tab has three pages: Members, Diplomacy and Chronicle. Only the Lord chooses the emblem and sets the guild's stances; the Lord and the Commanders invite, promote, demote and dismiss, and only they may plant a fallen standard again.

Invite a hunter by name. They must be online, and the invitation stands for three days; they accept or decline from their own book and come in at the lowest rank with room. Joining leaves a post in the Pit or the Host behind: nobody serves two masters.

The ranks keep the old chains' limits (ten Soldiers, six Captains, three Lieutenants, two Commanders, one Lord), but hired officers may hold only half of each: five, three, one and one. The throne is always a hunter's. A Commander may only raise or lower those below its own rank, and never up to it.

Promotions are yours to give. The guild only promotes on its own when a hired officer's place has stood open for two days, and then it raises one of your hired officers from the rank below; it never hires anyone new. Dismiss a hired officer and it goes back to the wild; dismiss a hunter and they are out.
Your hired officers roam out from the standard into your sectors of the front, and your Commanders keep watch beside the standard itself. While it is down, none of them shows itself.

Wild demons and angels judge you by your guild's stance toward their side. Members of one guild, and of allied guilds, cannot hurt each other; between hostile guilds, blades are drawn as far as the server allows fighting between hunters.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.guild_re: Only the Lord or a Commander may hire for the guild. Pay a wild demon, angel, fallen angel or rival hunter and it enters at rank I. A demon asks 16 sulfur and 8 gold ingots; an angel, 4 holy oil and 8 gold ingots; a fallen angel, 2 fallen blood and 8 gold ingots; a hunter, 16 emeralds and 8 salt.

An enemy officer of rank I–III may stake its service on a duel. Beat it and it deserts to your guild one rank lower, with rank I as the floor. Ask it to fight for its allegiance rather than simply killing it.

The binding rite is the costly third road: write the name of an officer of any rank up to IV and bind it to your guild. It keeps its rank. Every method needs a vacant NPC place at the resulting rank; at most half of any rank may be NPCs. Read Guild Diplomacy before bringing old enemies under one standard.

How to hire: carry the price, crouch and use a wild one. It names its price, and you pay it or walk away. How to win a deserter: crouch and use an enemy officer to parley, and ask it to fight for its allegiance. Not every temper takes the offer; one that does meets you in a ring until one of you yields.

How to bind: write the officer's name in a book, exactly as the Chain of Command tab spells it. Lay it on the altar of a small circle with two blocks of gold, two diamonds and an eye of ender, and light the rite with bound blood from the spell bowl. It costs 80 mana. A Lord, a Leviathan or an officer already in a duel cannot be bound.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.guild_st: Rename a vanilla banner on an anvil first: its name becomes the guild's name, 3–24 letters, digits, spaces or the marks ' - . &. After Lucifer's defeat, use that banner to activate the founding rite. It becomes a Guild Standard; planting it founds the guild.

Plant it in the Overworld, at least 300 blocks from the origin and at least 256 blocks from any other seat or standard. This is a seat you choose yourself; see Player Guilds for membership and command.

Enemies can break the standard. Without it the guild is homeless and its NPC officers do not appear. Raise it again within seven days: after that the guild loses its ground on the front. Replanting restores its seat.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.haunted_: In the forests and out on the plains stand old Victorian houses nobody will buy: a turret, a sagging porch, sheets over the furniture and a little family graveyard behind the fence. The family never left. Two to four of them walk its rooms at night.

Every ghost is bound to its bones, and here the bones are hidden: behind the cellar's shelves, in the graveyard, behind a false wall in the attic, at the bottom of the well, under the parlour floorboards. Find them, salt them, burn them, as you would any grave.
When the last of the family rests, the house falls quiet and a chest appears in the study: their keepsakes and a hunter's hidden notes, with a bowl page, sigil pages and silver.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.0: Heaven is not one place. Every soul that makes it up there gets a Heaven of its own: an island of its best days, in a light that never sets. Yours is waiting already. With Metatron fallen, nobody up there is keeping the door.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.1: Open a gate of light by day in a grace circle in the Overworld: a vial of Grace, two choir shards, two holy water, a golden apple and two feathers, woken with an angel blade (it is not used up). A frame of light stands over the altar for five minutes. Whoever crosses it lands in the Heaven of the hunter who opened it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.2: The first time, your island has to be written: give it a moment. You land on its plaza, by a gate of your own that never closes and always takes you back where you came in. From the plaza a lane of shrines leads off (Memory Lane, in this book), and past them stand a white wing behind a golden seal, a house with its door sealed shut, and a door that opens on a road.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.3: Nothing hurts you here. Fall off the edge and you wake on the plaza, whole. Nothing can be broken or built either, not until your home is yours; then your own yard is yours to change.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven.4: A General of the Host needs no gate: they ascend to their own island at will, with the friends who kneel beside them, and the same power takes them all back down the way they came.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven_g: Angels in dark suits and sunglasses, with a wire in one ear: Heaven's security. Naomi calls two or three at a time. While two of them stand she takes less from every blow, so cut them down first. They are only soldiers: a few good blows each.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heaven_h: When Zachariah's file is closed, the seal on the house's door burns away. It is yours: a room for your trophies, a store room whose chests open for you and the hunters you trust, and the hearth. From now on the yard round the house is yours to build on.

Rest by the hearth and you are mended: whole health, a full belly, every harm and every trace of Hell's torment gone, and a minute of regeneration besides. The fire needs ten minutes before it can do it again.
Coming home no longer needs the full rite. A smaller gate of light, opened at any hour once Zachariah has fallen, sets you down at your own front door.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heavenly: At the start of every phase, and every thirty seconds, he hands every hunter a Heavenly Form, numbered I to IV. While you hold one that is not filed, your blows against him are worth a quarter.

Four filing cabinets stand in his office, numbered I to IV. Use the form on the cabinet with its number and it is Approved: for ten seconds every blow you land on him counts half as much again. A clerk's Approval Stamp files any form at once.
Let a form run overdue and he notices: a smite comes down on you for it.
The form, and what files it
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heavens_: Zachariah's own seal of office. Carry it in your other hand, or as a charm: the first blow a great enemy lands on you in any minute is halved.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.heavy_we: The soul scythe is forged at night in a blood circle. Its swings reap a wide arc and drink some of the life they take. Hold use and let go for a crescent of souls.
The hellfire greatsword is slow and heavy. Hold use and let go to cleave a cone in front of you and leave a trail of hellfire behind it.
Both are tier III. The scythe also lights the rite that forges the Ring of Death.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hedge_wi: Not every witch is a crone over a cauldron. These ones walk the forests, swamps, taiga and plains at night, alone or in twos, and they work the same craft you do: sigils and the bowl. They keep six to fourteen blocks off and throw sigil bolts, mostly hexes that jinx you, now and then frost, and once in a while pain.

Get close and she will slip a curse bag into your pack; a protection bag on you turns it away. Hurt her badly and she drinks something foul and mends. Strike her up close and she may vanish in yellow smoke and come out of it eight to fourteen blocks away. Hurt one and every sister within sixteen blocks comes for you.

Left alone near a village, a hedge witch hexes villagers into her thralls, three at most in one place. And if her familiar steals a lock of your hair, she curses you with misfortune every thirty seconds, from wherever she is. A Ward of the Name or a protection bag turns the curse back on her; a Mirror Hex sends it home.
A witch killed by a hunter sometimes leaves a vial of her own blood: something of hers for the bowl.
A hedge witch, satchel full of someone else's hair
What she carries: taglocks, a page, now and then a vial of her blood
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.0: Only those who have beaten Lucifer can open the way. In the Overworld it takes the void circle and the Key, at night, with demon blood, embers, sulfur, a nether star and holy water.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.1: In the Nether it is cheaper: a great circle, two demon blood, two embers, sulfur and a blaze rod, lit with flint and steel at any hour.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.2: A rift stays open twenty minutes. Like the Nether, one step in Hell is eight up here, and the way back opens where you land. Lost down there? A binding circle in Hell with two salt, a holy water and brimstone tears a rift home, to your bed.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell.3: A King of Hell needs no rift: they descend at will, with the friends who kneel beside them, and the same power takes them all back up to where they sleep.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hell_reg: Hell is a roofed cavern world, like the Nether but taller. The Pit is at its heart; three regions lie around it.

The Ash Wastes burn hottest: brimstone in the rock. The Rack is wet with blood, and chains hang from its roof with meat hooks on the end. Crowley's Corridors are Hell as he ran it, an endless queue: a maze of stone corridors lined with barred cells, some keeping a chest, and in them, contracts.
Shards come from the walls of the Pit, fangs from hellhounds. Demons and occultists roam all of it, and the hounds hunt there in packs.

Hell gets into you. Torment grows while you stay, faster on the Rack, and fades once you leave: red at the edge of sight, whispers, shapes in the fog. It never hurts you. Salt in your off hand or a dash of holy water eases it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hellforg: An anvil, a blast furnace, two hellfire embers and two obsidian in a binding circle raise a Hellforge. It graves runes into weapons, and holds nothing itself.
Put the weapon in, and the runes beside it, as many as it has free slots. Grave costs the weapon's tier times two levels per rune. No more than two alike on one weapon.
Purge strips a weapon for one level and gives the runes back, all but one, lost at random. Think before you grave.

The slot at the far left takes an Ascension Shard. With the shard of the next tier there, Ascend raises the weapon (or a piece of Hunter's Gear, or of the General's armour) one tier, for five levels per tier.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hellhoun: You will not see them. Watch for the air that bends, the smoke of their breath, the paw prints that burn into the ground. They hunt in packs and their bite holds you where you stand.

Holy water, any holy wound or the Reveal sigil shows them for a while; Second Sight outlines them; the Eclipse Sight shows them always. They roam Hell, they come to collect on crossroads debts, and Lilith keeps a few.
Kill one and you may pull a fang. War and Death both want them.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.henry_wi: He knocked at dawn, the morning after the Devil fell: a polite young man in a brown suit and a fedora, a briefcase in his hand, who talks like a newsreel. Henry Winchester, a Legacy of the Men of Letters, out of 1958 and somehow standing in front of you.
He offers you a place in the order: a key, a bunker, and every secret the Men of Letters wrote down. Take it and you are an Aspirant; turn him down and he tips his hat and comes back in a few days.
Once you have joined he waits in the bunker's war room, by the lit map table. Talk to him there for a case. What the order knows is kept in the Archive, a tab of this book that only members have.
Henry Winchester, Legacy of the Men of Letters
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hex_bags: Witches' work. A curse bag tucked out of sight curses whoever lingers near it, all but the one who made it: bad luck, softer blows, a hunger that will not quit, and bleeding that gets worse the longer they stay. Now and then it draws worse: lightning, vermin, or after dark, a demon.

Set it down somewhere hidden, tuck it in a chest, or sneak up and slip it into someone's pocket. Found one? Only fire breaks it: flint and steel, a fire charge, any flame that reaches it, or a Purification.

A protection bag in your pack keeps the lesser demons from seeking you out unless you strike first, and no curse bag can touch you. It wears thin while demons are near, and crumbles to dust in the end.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hexed_in: Enochian ink steeped in one school's magic: pour in a potion, add the ink and something to steep it in. A gold nugget steeps it Enochian, blaze powder Infernal, an amethyst shard Witchcraft, salt Hunter. Nothing to steep in, nothing to brew.

Write a page of your grimoire while you carry hexed ink of that spell's school and the Scriptorium uses it instead of plain ink. The page remembers: a spell of that school cast from it is 15% stronger. Rewrite the page and the ink is spent again.
The Enochian orb is forged with one vial of hexed ink, of any school, in place of a second plain one.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hexed_vi: Hollow eyes, a shambling walk, weak swings at whoever comes near. Somebody's neighbour, under a witch's hex. You find them near covens, in abandoned churches, and near villages where a hedge witch has been at work.
You can kill one. Do that and its hex passes to you: jinxed and bad luck for two minutes, and nothing to show for it but rotten flesh.

Or free it. A salt round does it, and so does Break Hex: cast at it by name, or with it standing by the bowl. It slumps, straightens, and is a villager again, the very villager it was if a witch hexed one. It presses one to three emeralds on you and tells the village what you did.
A villager under a witch's hex
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.holy_oil: The one fire an angel fears. Pour it on the ground and it runs out in a ring two blocks wide and catches at once: an angel inside cannot leave until it burns out, and one who crosses the flames is burned.
Holy oil set alight is the one fire an angel cannot cross. Raphael's house has rings of it poured on the floor, dark and glossy: four of them, squares of oil round a patch of bare boards.

Set a ring alight while he stands inside it, with flint and steel, a fire charge or a burning arrow, and he is held there for six seconds: he cannot strike, cannot heal, and takes more from every blow. Then the ring burns out, and for a while no other ring will hold him.
He knows the oil and walks round it, but he does not think about it when he blinks or when he smites: lure him there. Lit or not, the rings are poured again at the start of every phase.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.holy_wat: Three bottles of water and a pinch of salt on a ritual altar, inside a small chalk ring, lit with flint and steel: three flasks of holy water. That is the first rite any hunter learns.
Throw it like a splash potion. It scalds demons. It scatters a ghost for a while. It shows a hellhound for what it is. In Hell, a dash of it eases the Torment.
You will pour more of it into rites and bowls than you ever throw. Make it by the dozen.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.horseman: Every time a Horseman falls his horse stays behind: red for War, black for Famine, sickly pale for Pestilence, pale as bone for Death. They have no powers, but they are better horses than any you could breed: tougher, faster, and they jump higher. Tame one, saddle it and ride.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.host_of_: Angels in their vessels, in suits, trench coats and fatigues, with breastplates, angel blades and tower shields: Michael's soldiers. They march in ranks and obey their captain, the one with the plumed helm and its wings open. While it stands they hold together; when it falls they break.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hosts_an: A General of the Host calls down a squad: a captain and four soldiers who follow you, fight what you fight and go back to Heaven after a minute.
A soldier of the Host, at a General's side
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hound_wh: Lilith keeps her dogs on a whistle, and she drops it when she dies. Blow it and a hellhound runs at your side for a minute, for a little mana.
Yours you can see. It goes for whatever hurts you and whatever you strike, and it never turns on a player. One at a time.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.how_an_a: Put an angel blade through one and you'll see it: the angel locks up, and the light comes out of its eyes and its mouth, brighter and brighter, with a sound like a scream through glass. Then a flash, and it drops. Its wings stay behind, burnt into the ground.

Any angel blade does it: the one you forge, Zachariah's, Gabriel's, Lucifer's own. Any other weapon still hurts one, but it takes five times the work, and they don't die like that. Their own blades kill each other the same way, if you are there to watch.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hungry_t: The First Blade. A great circle at night, lit with Ruby's knife: two bone blocks, three demon blood, a netherite ingot, a wither skeleton skull and a hellfire ember. It is bound to whoever forged it, and burns anyone else who holds it.

Feed it kills and it grows: at the third level it lets you lunge, and at the fifth, well fed, it will not let you die. Starve it and it feeds on you. It whispers. Do not listen. In the hand of one who bears the Mark of Cain it never hungers and strikes three times as hard.

The Whispering Codex is the same hunger in a book: a cursed catalyst, bound to its maker. Spells cast through it cost blood and sanity instead of mana, and they chain and pierce. Alone, it speaks the Forbidden Word, and whatever it marks takes more harm.
Watch your sanity with the Codex in hand. When it runs low, the words twist.
Famine's starving thralls. They pay you no mind: they shuffle to their master to be eaten, and every one that reaches him heals him. Kill them on the way.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hunter_r: A hunter who stays human can still rise: three ranks, each sworn at the altar. Only a human sworn to no side may take the oath, and choosing Heaven or Hell later gives the hunter's ranks up.

Hunter: the oath, sworn over a Colt bullet, four salt, two holy waters and a silver machete; your mana runs deeper (25 more for each rank). Veteran: a night's vigil over Lilith's and Metatron's trophies; supernatural things within 24 blocks glow faintly to you. Legend: the four Horsemen's rings and a Fallen Star; your hunter's weapons strike the supernatural a fifth harder, and possession slides off you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hunters_: Two strings, a gold ingot, and a drop of demon blood in the middle. It grows warm when something supernatural comes within sixteen blocks of you, and it steadies your hand: every kind of magic, sigil, bowl or rite, costs a tenth less mana while you wear it.
Wear it around your neck if you have the slot for it (Curios), or keep it in your hotbar or off hand.
Sneak and use your grimoire and the whole book opens. Four ribbons down the edge: Home, Journal, Scriptorium and Roadmap.

Home is the state of you: mana, sanity, what has changed you, any deal you owe on, and the next thing worth hunting. The Journal is these pages; mark the ones you need with a ribbon. The Scriptorium is where spells are composed, written into the grimoire or onto scrolls, and kept in a library for later.
The Roadmap is the long road from salt to the Cage, every hunt that matters laid out in order. What you have not found yet is a shadow on it.

A cap, a canvas jacket over flannel, jeans and work boots. Nothing an angel would look at twice, which is the point. Leather, iron and salt sewn into the seams, at any crafting table; about as tough as iron.
It ascends at the Hellforge like a weapon, up to IV. Each tier hardens it (at IV the whole set is as hard as armour gets) and gives it Aegis.

Aegis turns aside part of every blow a great enemy deals, even their Divine Wrath, the share of their blows that no armour, enchantment, potion or shield stops. A whole set gives 5% at I, 10% at II, 15% at III and 20% at IV; each piece a quarter of that. The General's armour is born at IV, and a fifth shard raises it to V: 30%, the hardest armour there is.

Your side adds to it. An angel gains 5% Aegis and two armour for each rank; a demon, two hearts for each rank; a hunter, a heart for each rank, and 5% Aegis against Divine Wrath. Aegis never turns aside more than 60%. Lesser creatures, and the enemies' own servants, are not great enough for it to matter.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.hymnal_s: High on the mountains stand ruins of white stone, a stair winding up to a broken platform on the peak. To find one, draw a Hymnal Map: a small circle, a compass, a feather, a gold ingot, an amethyst shard and a holy water on the altar, and a blank map to light it.

Halfway up the stair stands a temple. Its window keeps the hymn, three panes read left to right, and its chest always keeps a Shattered Hymn, with holy water, salt, ink and, if you are lucky, a few of the Colt's rounds.
On the summit wait the Choir Altar and its seven bells. In a storm, the altar's light reaches the clouds. Read the Broken Chorus's page before you ring anything.

The choir did not live on the peak alone. On a ledge of the slope stands their monastery, cloister, refectory and cells, its scriptorium still holding pages; under it or the temple sleep the choristers, in a crypt whose chest keeps the old vault's gold. Look out too for the fallen belfry and its cracked bell, and for the lookouts off the stair.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.kept_mem: Memories that belong together are worth more together. Gather a whole set and it stays with you, wherever you go.

Victories: five great enemies' falls make you a little harder to hurt by great enemies (+3% Aegis); every one of them, a heart more. The Crossroads: your deals' terms run a day longer. Cases: research runs a little faster at the desks. Kin: a deeper well of mana. Companions: your tamed pets close by heal over time. Sightings: ten first sightings, and you strike a little harder at every kind of creature you have seen (never the great enemies).
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.key_to_t: The Key is forged, not found. A great circle, at night: a nether star, four hellfire embers, a gold block and two vials of Azazel's own blood. Nothing else will do for the blood. He has to fall first.

The Key lights the rite that opens the Cage, and later, the rifts that lead down into Hell. Lose to what is in the Cage and he leaves a cracked key behind him; a great circle at night, two embers and a demon blood make it whole again.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.killing_: Bobby's notes, copied out clean. One: find it. In a village after Raphael's fall, distrust anyone too eager to hand you a free burger. Second Sight or the Spellwright's Spectacles show the maw under the face; a splash of borax does it for anyone. Do not eat what they hand out: a sedated hunter cannot see them.

Two: burn it. Ordinary blows land for a third and it knits back a heart every two seconds. Borax (thrown, rubbed in, or Leviathan's Bane) burns it for ten seconds: no knitting, and every blow lands in full. Keep it burning.
Three: take the head. At half its health or less, a sword or an axe through the neck takes the head off. The body drops. Do not stop there.

Four: finish the head. It crawls home on its tongue; if it gets there, the Leviathan stands up again. Bag it with an empty hand, burn it, borax it, or knock it twelve blocks off and keep it there for five seconds.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.knights_: Abaddon's own blade, left to whoever beats her the first time: a tier IV cursed cleaver. Use it and a wave of hellfire runs nine blocks down the ground before you, setting what it finds alight; then it needs six seconds. Without the Mark it hungers like the First Blade.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.last_sea: Sixty-six seals held the Cage shut, and Lilith was the last. When she dies, it breaks, and what is left of it falls at your feet.
Lucifer's summoning will not take without it, and the rite burns it. If he wins, the seal is gone with him: you will be calling Lilith up again before you get another try.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.leviatha: The first beasts God made, locked in Purgatory before there was anything else. When Raphael fell they came out with him, and now they walk the villages in borrowed faces: at night one takes a villager nobody is looking at and wears its face, three to a village at most.

In a borrowed face it keeps to itself and hands out free samples of SucroCorp food. Second Sight or the Spellwright's Spectacles show it for what it is, and so does any blow: its head splits into a maw full of teeth and it hunts anyone who is not sedated.

Ordinary harm barely touches one (about a third of every blow), and it knits back a heart every two seconds. Borax burns it and stops the knitting for ten seconds; while it burns, every blow lands in full. The Men of Letters send hunters to villages they hold, too.
A Leviathan, its head split open

The laboratory coat is another borrowed skin. SucroCorp's chemists work where the black goo meets the food supply, and serve the Board beyond the laboratories too. They see a village as a trial batch and a hunter as a sample. Borax is your answer.
A chemist from the SucroCorp laboratories

A suit, a measured smile and an appetite older than civilisation. The executives serve the Board in its tower and its officers' escorts. Never mistake a corporate title for an offer to talk. Bring borax.
An executive in a borrowed skin

SucroCorp security protects the food supply from anything that fights back. These guards serve in the tower and the officers' escorts. Human, angel or demon, an intruder is meat. Keep borax ready when the borrowed face opens.
A guard on the Board's payroll

A shard of the Word of God, the tablet that tells how the Leviathans end. Read, it teaches Leviathan's Bane (second tier, Hunter): a burst of borax that burns whatever borax burns and dries the goo where it lands.
Roman Enterprises' sprayer comes with it: a cone of borax five blocks long, forty-eight puffs; sneak and use it with borax in your pack to refill sixteen a box.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lilith.0: The first demon. She only answers once Azazel is dead: a great circle at night, three demon blood, two hellfire embers, two bones and a vial of bound blood to sign her contract.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lilith.1: Headstones rise in a ring around the circle. When she shines, the white light falls on everyone she can see: put a headstone between you. Each one takes two bursts before it falls, so keep moving. After each burst she is hollow for a moment, and that is when to hit her. In the end her light comes twice.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lilith.2: If she writes your name, it is a contract. Everyone who can must wound her before it comes due, and holy wounds pay it down twice as fast. Burn it in time and she staggers. Fail, and hounds you cannot see come for whoever she named.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.linger_a: Two modifiers of the second tier from the bunker library. Each makes the spell cost half as much again.
Linger leaves a zone where the spell first takes hold: for four seconds it repeats the spell every second at half strength on whatever stands in it. One zone per cast.
Quicken lets your hand recover faster: the spell's wait, whichever of its sigils sets it, is cut by two fifths.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.locating: The smoke drifts toward what you seek and tells you which way, and roughly how far. What you put in the bowl decides what it looks for.
If what you seek is in another world, or nowhere at all, the smoke sinks back and the bowl keeps its contents.
To open the Cage: the great circle, at night, lit with the Key. Three demon blood, two hellfire embers, a holy water and the Last Seal on the altar.

Only holy things truly hurt him: angel blades, Smite, holy water. The Cage will not let you leave. Every attack is written on the ground first: red is fire, so move; blue is frost; violet is a beam, so break line of sight; gold is judgement. Hit hardest while he recovers after an attack.
He has four faces before the end: Lucifer, the Fallen, the Morningstar, and the Archangel Unbound, who takes to the air. If he wins, he walks back into the Cage and leaves a cracked key behind.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lucifer_: At the heart of Hell the Pit falls to the lava sea, and over it the Cage hangs on its chains. Under it, on the island, is the dais: draw the circle around its four stones, lay the four rings with two demon blood, a holy water and an ember, and open the Cage with the Key. He comes down in chains, and leaves them behind, one by one.

Six faces. The Prisoner. Hellfire. The cold of the Cage. Legion: kill the hounds, or they will drag you down. The Morning Star: watch for gold on the ground, the stars are falling. Light-Bringer: stand between the wings, and when he burns, find the green. Everything you learned against him still holds, but the floor will not.
If you fall, the rings stay on the stone. Beat him and the Cage is shut, and what he leaves behind is a fallen star, a load of rounds, two nether stars and a page of Smite.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.lucifers: When Lucifer falls, a shard of his grace falls with him. Use it to take it in. Light pours into you, and it does not leave.
Your mana runs fifty deeper, for good. And the third-tier sigils, the pages written in the hand that burned your eyes, become legible. Echo among them.
You only get to carry one shard. The rest are no use to you; give them to someone who hunts with you.
A shard of an archangel's grace
Jump the shockwave when he lands. Break out of an ice cage with any tool. Hide behind ice from the grace beam. Reveal unmasks his illusions; strike one and it bursts.
The Snare only holds him while he recovers. When he gathers his grace, stand in a green sigil or inside a Ward, or die. Break his grace tether by running or by hitting him.
Beat him and he leaves everything: the Archangel Blade, his grace, the Colt and rounds for it, a nether star, the Echo sigil, and his likeness in stone.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.mana_and: Every sigil and every rite draws on your mana. You start with a hundred and it seeps back on its own, a couple of points a second. The blue bar shows where you stand.
It can run deeper. An archangel's grace adds fifty for good; the Darkness's mark adds twenty-five; a crossroads deal will sell you twenty-five more, at the usual price.

Sanity is the other bar, and most hunters never see it move. Some cursed things are paid for in your mind. Let it run low and you will hear whispers, and the words start to twist in your mouth. It comes back slowly on its own; a Purification steadies it at once.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.marks_of: What the witchcraft leaves on a body, as your own eyes will show it.

Agony: a pulse of harm every two seconds that stops at half a heart. Rot: now and then a bite of food in your pack turns to rotten flesh. Silenced: no sigil will come and no power answers. Marked: everything hurts a fifth more. Compelled: you follow, or you are drawn.
Name-Warded and Mirrored are the protections. Silver Edge counts down the silver blows you have left.
