Each school trains on its own. A sigil teaches a fifth of the mana it cost; a bowl spell twice that for the same mana; a rite a third of its mana. Practice what you mean to be good at. Mastery stays with you through death.
An Apprentice (150) reads that school's second-tier pages, pays 5% less for its magic and has 5 more mana.
An Adept (600) reads third-tier pages, pays 10% less and has 10 more mana.
A Master (1800) reads a Master's pages, pays 15% less and has 20 more mana. Only your highest rank in any school adds mana: ranks in four schools do not add up to more.

Discounts add together and never take off more than 40%: being human saves 15% on all magic, the Hunter's Amulet 10%, and your rank in the spell's school the rest. A scroll still halves what is left on top of that.
A page beyond you stays unread, and you keep it. A page of no school, a form or a modifier, wants the rank in any school. What you have learned is never taken away.
Morningstar's Spark, what is left in you after you take in Lucifer's grace, reads every page as an Adept would. That is how Echo is read by those who never studied.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.memories: Heaven remembers your road even if you don't. The fall of every great enemy, every deal at the crossroads, every case closed or lost, every rank you rose to, the pets you buried, the first time you saw each creature and the one you hunted most: all of it is kept, even what happened before you ever came up here.

Twelve shrines line the lane, each holding one memory behind a shimmering veil. Step through a veil and the memory is staged before you, in the hollow at the end of the lane: the place as it was, the people as they stood. One of them glows. Touch it, and the memory is gathered: it gets its own page in the Memories tab of this book.

Walk out through the veil at the stage's edge, or stay away long enough, and the stage clears for the next. Only one memory plays at a time. The shrines show what you have not gathered first; once you have them all, others take their turn.
Gather three memories and the golden seal over the white wing opens. Somebody works in there.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.men_of_l: A brotherhood of scholars who watched the dark and wrote it all down, so that hunters could put it to rest. Angels, demons and plain hunters alike may join: the order cares what you know, not what you are.

Ranks are earned at the research desks. Aspirant on joining; Initiate after five pieces of research (the Men of Letters Ring: research runs a tenth faster); Scholar after fifteen, of three kinds (the Spellwright's Spectacles: worn, they show what hides); Master of Letters after thirty-five, of four kinds (Henry's Case: nine pockets for artifacts); Keeper of the Lore after seventy, of five kinds (the Aquarian Star: one more research at a time).
A member's book grows a tab no outsider ever sees: the Archive, where everything the order learns is kept.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.metatron: The Scribe of God. Once the Broken Chorus is silenced, write his name, Metatron, in a book and quill, and offer it in a great circle at night with two choir shards, a chrism, a holy water, two feathers and a glow ink sac.

He fights with a blade at first. Then his Hand writes burning words across the floor: get out of the strokes before they burn, jump the sweep, be elsewhere when the palm comes down. In the third act he takes to a lectern on a dais with two flights of stairs and will not leave it; climb, or strike from afar. His Book crushes, storms pages, and shuts on one of you until the others wound him enough.
At the last he takes up the Tablet and speaks the Word: BE STILL, LOOK AWAY or KNEEL. Obey it, to the letter, for the three seconds it holds. Watch the sky, too: angels fall burning where he points.
The eldest archangel, Heaven's general, and Lucifer's brother: the end of Heaven's road as Lucifer Uncaged is the end of Hell's. Once Metatron has fallen, call him down by day in a great circle in the Overworld with the Angel Tablet, the Seraph Wings, three choir shards and two holy waters, woken with an angel blade. Win or lose, the Tablet and the Wings fall back to earth.

He comes down into a Garden of Heaven wearing his vessel, a young man in a grey suit, and fights with an angel blade. When his palm starts to shine, never let it reach your brow: break his reach or turn it with a shield. He will ask you for your yes. Say it, and for a while he wears you: your body walks to your friends and burns them, and he heals; when he lets go, his grace stays with you and your blows land twice as hard on him. Say no, or say nothing, and the Host of Heaven hunts you.

Then the Host of Heaven takes the field, in ranks behind its captain; strike the captain down and they break. In the War in Heaven his shadow spreads its wings: his lance pins whoever it strikes and stays in the ground until he calls it back (he is quicker without it, but his reach is short). Then he takes to the sky with storms of steel feathers and dives; when he lands to gather himself, strike.

In the Throne Room his vessel burns away and his true form stands up: a general in white and gold, four blocks and more, six wings of steel and a halo of spears. When the halo breaks, his lance can be pulled from the ground and thrown back at him.
What he leaves, for every hunter, every time
And one piece of his armour you do not have yet
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.michaels: Lucifer's brother's grace. Take it in, once, and it stays with you. Wear the Seraph Wings on your back (or in your chest slot) and they will carry you as freely as a bird, for as long as their strength lasts; run them dry in the air and they fold, and you drift down. Touch the ground to let them rest.
The one weapon an archangel fears from another. Throw it and it comes back to your hand; it strikes angels and demons twice as hard and pins what it strikes for a moment.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.name_war: Protection is laid on you, or on whoever a taglock in the bowl names. It needs no blood.
Under a Ward of the Name every curse and binding aimed at you fails, and stings whoever spoke it; scrying shows them nothing; Hex and the curse bags slide off you.
A Mirror Hex sends the next curse back to its caster and breaks. A caster under their own Ward shrugs off what comes back.
Ward of the Name: ten minutes
Mirror Hex: twenty minutes, or until it breaks
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.0: When an angel starts asking questions, Heaven sends it to Naomi. She sits it in a chair, puts a drill to its eye and keeps going until the questions stop; then she sends it back to work. A calm, severe woman in a grey suit and a white coat, she has run that room for longer than humans have had words.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.1: Her room is the white wing of your own Heaven. Its seal opens once you have gathered three memories; walk in and she is waiting, with the chairs, the console and the guards. There is no rite. Nobody else's road needs her: she is a challenge, not a duty.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.2: I. Intake. Her open palm comes down in a gold circle (raise a shield as it lands and she staggers); a gold ring holds whoever stands in it. A line runs from a chair to whoever stands most alone: if it catches you, you are strapped in (The Chair, in this book). She lunges with the drill in a cone and leaves you bleeding. A white ring spreads from her to wipe your mind: step into its green gaps, or see nothing for a while and move slowly after.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.3: She calls her guards, and while two of them stand she takes less from every blow. She stages a training test with copies of the people you love (The Training Test, in this book). When she is hurt she walks to the console and heals herself until somebody strikes it six times.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.4: II. Reprogramming. At half her strength the room changes round you and she stops being patient: the drill lunges three times in a row, and the chair holds harder.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.5: An angel of the second rank or more is the first one she straps in: you are one of hers, and you should sit. A demon feels the drill more.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.6: Once she has fallen, the room stays quiet when you walk in. Crouch as you cross into it to call her back.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.7: Met again, she leaves her bust, and now and then her drill or her diadem. Like every great enemy, she also leaves a shard for the Hellforge and, the first time, a heart of Vitality. And the lift at the back of her room starts working.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomi.ca: What she leaves the first time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.naomis_d: A thin band of white gold she wore to keep her own head clear. Carry it in your other hand, or as a charm: nothing can condition you, mark you for Heaven or possess you, and great enemies hurt you a little less (+3% Aegis).

The drill she used on angels for a thousand years: a holy weapon of the fourth tier. Strike the same creature three times and its will is yours: for ten seconds it fights for you. It never works on a great enemy. Raise it at the Hellforge and it holds them longer.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.nw_conse: In a world with Nations & War, a guild is a nation. Found a town and a nation there first; then, as your nation's leader, perform the founding rite as usual and plant the Guild Standard in your capital. Your nation becomes one of the world's four guilds, and you sit on its throne as Lord.

The ring of sectors is gone: your guild's ground is your nation's land, claimed and defended in Nations & War. The standard must stand on your own land; if your nation loses the chunk it stands on, it comes down as if broken.

Your guild's stance towards another guild-nation follows your nations: allied in Nations & War means allied here, at war means hostile, anything else neutral. Towards the Pit, the Host and SucroCorp you keep your own stance, as before.

A guild founded before Nations & War keeps its old ways (its standard planted anywhere the spacing allows, members by invitation) until its Lord, leading a nation, plants the standard again in that nation's capital. Then the nation is consecrated as the guild, and every member it had keeps their place even if they are not citizens.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.nw_domin: The Pit, the Host and SucroCorp appear in Nations & War as nations of their own. Nobody joins them, allies with them or rules them there: their people and ranks are in this book. Open their card in the nation menu while you carry the Hunter's Book to come straight here.

Each holds its seat (the stronghold's ground, reserved but as open to raiders as ever) and a few enclaves: small shrines out in the world with a Town Core at their heart. Their officers roam out from those towns. Enclaves are won and lost in war; a power never raises a lost enclave again by itself.

In a world that already had the ring of sectors, each power's enclaves stand in the sectors it held (up to six, nearest its seat). An enclave never takes land someone has built on: it moves further along its bearing.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.nw_incur: A power hostile to a guild-nation may declare an incursion at dawn. It is a Nations & War war: when it turns active the power's war parties march on your frontier with a Siege Banner whenever your people are near. Its officers, its garrisons and any hunter who holds a post in its chain fight on its side.

Win, and the power is shaken and loses an enclave. Lose, and your nation becomes its vassal for a few days: it takes a tribute from your bank, you cannot make war on it, and your guild is at peace with it until the service ends.
Every citizen of a consecrated nation may swear the oath from the guild's record in the Chain of Command tab; no invitation is needed, and only citizens may join. Swearing leaves any post you held in the Pit or the Host behind.

The oath is your choice: a citizen who never swears may keep a post in the Pit or the Host, even while living in a nation that is their foe. Leave the nation and you leave the guild. When the nation's leader changes, the throne follows them once they have sworn.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.nw_seat_: A guild-nation hostile to a power may declare war on it from Nations & War. Besiege its enclaves, or carry a Siege Banner to its seat. When the seat's heart chunk falls, the Lord's hall lies open, but the seat has no Town Core: it falls only when its Lord falls to your side.
A seat is never taken. The power loses enclaves instead, is shaken, and its dead Lord leaves an empty throne for its court to fight over.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.nw_war_o: When Heaven and Hell go to war, it is a Nations & War war between their nations. Skirmishes, champions' duels and slain hunters still score; their parties besiege each other's enclaves, and hunters of either side may join the fight. An enclave that falls changes masters and its shrine is rebuilt in the winner's colours.
When the war ends, the winner takes ground even without a siege won: the loser's enclave nearest the winner's seat goes over to it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.on_angel: Forget the halos. An angel is a soldier, old as the world and twice as proud, and most of what hurts a demon does nothing to one. Salt, traps and exorcism: no.
Holy things are what works. Angel blades, the Smite sigil, holy water, a Sanctity rune graven in your weapon. Watch the ground, too: everything an archangel does is written on it first.
The ones in this book: Lucifer in his Cage, the Broken Chorus over the mountains, and Metatron, who writes everything down.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.penumbra: Penumbra, the blade that drinks the light, left by the Darkness. It drinks light from bright places and from lit foes. Hold use and let go for an Umbra Wave that blinds and wounds, stronger the more light it holds. It cuts deeper in the dark.

The Eclipse Sight is a vial of her own sight. Drink it and you are marked for good: darkness and blindness cannot take you, the eclipse cannot hide the world, hellhounds are plain to see, and your mana runs twenty-five deeper.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.pestilen: Sickly, coughing, with glasses and a cane, and sorry for nothing. Call him with a fermented spider eye, mushrooms and clotted blood, once Lucifer has fallen. His ground is a toxic swamp.

Toxic clouds grow over the swamp and everything he does gives you the plague. Then the flies come: swarms that chase and blind and only burn. On his sickly horse he leaves a trail of plague and coughs cones of it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.pet_coll: Leather, string and an iron nugget. Use the collar on a tamed animal of yours and it wears the twin of it; the one in your hand is the link.
With the collar in the bowl you can find a lost pet, and the collar comes back to you. If the worst has happened, there is a spell for that too.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.plague.0: Pestilence's plague stacks up to five times. Every stack eats a little more of you, takes a heart off your health while it lasts and stops you healing on your own. It does not wear off by itself while he keeps giving it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.plague.1: While he fights, antidote vials turn up in dry spots of his swamp. Drink one: the plague is gone and none takes for fifteen seconds.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.plague.2: His flies only burn: hit them with a Fire Aspect blade or a burning arrow, light them with flint and steel, lead them through fire, or walk into them burning.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.player_g: After killing Lucifer, any hunter may found a guild: human, demon or angel. At most four may stand in a world. Choose a name, colour and emblem of your own; your standard is your seat, and you are its Lord.

Invite hunters from the Chain of Command tab of the Hunter's Book; they answer there too. Membership is exclusive: joining a guild leaves your post in the Pit or the Host. A hunter cannot serve two guilds.

A guild has the same ranks as the older chains, but hired NPCs may fill only half the places at each rank. The remaining places belong to hunters. See Recruiting for paid service, duels and binding, and Guild Interregnum for what happens when the Lord is gone.
Raphael, the archangel who heals and the archangel who smites. With the Horsemen loose and Lucifer free, he means to finish the Apocalypse his brothers started. He wears a tall, stern man in a dark suit and a long black coat, and he only comes down in a thunderstorm.

Wait for thunder, then lay two holy oils, a lightning rod, a glistering melon, a golden apple and two feathers in a grace circle in the Overworld, after War, Famine and Pestilence are beaten, and wake it with an angel blade (it is not used up). He comes down in a bolt where the altar stood, and an old abandoned house stands round you. The storm will not lift until it is over. Nobody else's road needs him: he is a challenge, not a duty.

I. The Storm. Inside the house he calls lightning on you (a violet mark on the floor first: move), claps thunder that throws you back, blinks from place to place with a flinch of wings, and sends bolts through the broken windows in lines. When he raises his hand and it burns, he is about to smite: hit him hard enough, or catch the blow on a raised shield, and the smite breaks.

II. The Healer. He calls his garrison, and each angel holds a thread of grace to him that heals him while it lasts. Stand in a thread to cut it, or cut the angel down; once, he lays his hands on a fallen one and raises it. (His Garrison, in this book.)

III. Wrath of Heaven. He tears the roof off the house. Lightning falls in fields and leaps from one of you to the next, every flash throws the shadow of his wings across the walls, and his veins burn with light. When he snaps his fingers the air bursts all round him: only a green band halfway out is safe.
All through the fight there are rings of holy oil on the floor. Light one with him inside it and the storm is yours for a moment. (The Holy Oil Trap, in this book.)
Called again, he leaves his trophy, and now and then his staff. Like every great enemy, he also leaves a shard for the Hellforge and, the first time, a heart of Vitality.
What he leaves the first time
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.raphaels: A tall staff of black wood bound in silver, crowned with a cage that holds a crystal of the storm. It is a holy catalyst of the fourth tier: your sigils cast through it.

Its own spell is lightning that leaps from foe to foe, up to three of them near you. Sneak as you use it and it lays a healing grace on you and your allies close by instead; that needs a while before it answers again. Both grow with its Ascension at the Hellforge.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reaper.0: In Death's fight every hunter carries a clock of about a minute, a pocket watch in the corner of the eye. Hitting Death or killing a reaper winds it back to full. A reaper's touch takes time off it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reaper.1: Reapers are only seen by those whose time is nearly up (under twenty seconds), by those in limbo, and by everyone once the world of the dead holds the arena.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reaper.2: When a clock runs out its hunter falls into limbo: the world goes grey and only the reapers and a light remain. Reach the light within fifteen seconds and you walk back out. Otherwise, you die.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.red_hand: Now you have seen one with your own eyes: a neighbour's face sliding off like a wet paper bag, and the maw underneath. They are patient. They take one villager at a time, at night, when nobody is looking — and sometimes when somebody is.
Count the villagers. A village never loses its last two to them, and never holds more than three at once: if the baker has stopped sleeping and keeps offering you sandwiches, you know where to start.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.reprogra: A white leather chair with straps at the wrists and ankles, and over it, on a jointed arm, the drill. When her line catches you, you are in it, and you cannot get up.

Struggle: press jump as fast as you can. Eighteen good pulls in four seconds break the straps; in her second phase it takes twenty-four in three and a half. A human's will makes it easier; an angel was made to sit still, and it is harder. A friend can free you with three blows to the chair.

Fail, and the drill comes down: a twentieth of your strength and more, through any armour, and for a few seconds you are Conditioned (your blows against angels fall soft). She heals a little, and lets you go.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.research: Sit at a research desk and the order's board offers you topics: formulas (new sigils for the grimoire), rites (new bowl spells), the identity of a cursed artifact, a creature's file, a great enemy's file, the write-up of a solved case, and the Archive's own lore. Higher tiers open with higher ranks.

Each costs field notes of its kind, paper and ink. Field notes come from the creatures you kill as a member, from chests in the world's ruins and from solved cases. Research runs on game time, even while you are away; when it is done, its page is in the Archive.

You never carry field notes: they go straight into your Archive, and the desk takes them from there. The Archive's Field Notes shelf counts what you have, and each creature's file says how many you hold on it. Loose notes someone else left lying about are filed the moment you pick them up or use them.
A creature's file has no end: every level adds to your damage against that kind of creature (never against the great enemies), less with each level.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.righteou: Only one thing kills the head of the Leviathans: the bone of a righteous mortal, washed in the blood of three who fell: a fallen angel, a King of Hell and an Alpha.

The bone is a nun's, kept in the crypt chest of an abandoned church. Raphael leaves his own blood (and the page to work it); a crossroads demon killed in a fight may leave a King's; a vampire, now and then, an Alpha's.
The bone and the three bloods
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rite_of_: Done at the altar, on a full bar, and it takes all of it. Each Deepening adds 50 to your mana for good, and there is no end to how deep the well goes; only to how fast.
The first five are drawn in a plain chalk square round the altar: one amethyst shard and one vial of Enochian ink, lit with flint and steel.
The next five want a devil's trap, chalk with a lit candle at each corner, and twice the offerings.

From the eleventh on, and for ever after: the grace circle, chalk round the altar with four lit white candles inside, four of each offering, and Lucifer's grace in place of the flint, burnt by the rite.

After each Deepening the well settles: a day after the first, then two, then four, then eight, and never longer. The Wellspring settles on its own, so the two can be taken turn about. Try the wrong form, too soon, or half-empty, and the altar tells you why and takes nothing.
Spoken over the spell bowl, on a full bar, and it takes all of it. The bowl will not take the words until you have read the Wellspring's page, which turns up like any other spell page.
Everyone's mana comes back at 2% of the bar a second. Each Wellspring adds 1% more, without end: ten of them and a bar refills in under nine seconds.

The first five take one dose of holy water and one choir shard; the next five two of each; from the eleventh on four of each and a vial of Azazel's blood. Each form has its own words, and they grow longer.
After each Wellspring the bowl's well settles: a day, then two, four, and eight at most. The Deepening rests on its own.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rites_of: The angel's ranks, from the first Grace to the Host. Each needs the rank before it.
The demon's ranks after the crossroads. Each needs the rank before it.
The hunter's oaths, and the rites that undo a side and bless the ground.
Mana is a well, and a well can be dug deeper. Two rites do it, as often as you can bear them, and each takes your whole bar: come to them full, and leave empty.
The Rite of Deepening is done at the altar, with amethyst and Enochian ink. Each one adds 50 to your mana for good.
The Rite of the Wellspring is spoken over the spell bowl, with holy water and choir shards, once its page is read. Your mana comes back at 2% of your bar a second, and each Wellspring adds 1% more.

Each rite has three forms. The first five take one of each offering; the next five twice as many; from the eleventh on, twice that again and a great enemy's spoil: Lucifer's grace lights the Deepening, Azazel's blood goes in the bowl. After each rite the well settles for a day, then two, four, and eight at most, each rite on its own.
Every tenth rite, of either kind, brings a title: Deepened, Wellspring-born, Fathomless, Abyss-deep and, past fifty, Boundless.
Each rite has its own page: the Rite of Deepening among the rituals, the Rite of the Wellspring among the bowl's spells.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.ritual_c: The small circle: eight chalk lines around the altar, nothing else. The binding circle: a 5x5 chalk square with a lit candle on each corner. The blood circle is the same square drawn in blood chalk.

The great circle is the one for summonings: a ring of blood chalk nine wide, with six lit black candles inside it. The void circle is a ring of the same size broken by crying obsidian at its four points, with four black candles close around the altar.
There is one more circle, drawn only around four old stones under the Cage in Hell. If you ever need it, you will know.
Blood chalk: four chalk and a demon's blood
Chalk, blood chalk, black candle, crying obsidian
Every rite starts with an altar: polished blackstone bricks, a gold ingot and a candle. Set it down, and draw the circle the rite asks for around it, on the same level, with chalk lines and candles lit where it wants them.

Lay the offerings on the altar one at a time, then light the rite with what it asks for, flint and steel more often than not. Some rites want the night, some the day, some a certain place. The rite takes its mana up front.

If the circle is wrong, red sparks mark the first bad block. Once it is burning, never smudge a line or snuff a candle: the circle breaks, lightning falls, it burns you, and something comes through that should not.

A rite that cannot be answered spends nothing: if another fight already holds the world, the summoning is refused before it starts and the altar says where that fight is; if nothing answers in the end, what lit it comes back to you.

The keys of the road (the Last Seal, the Key to the Cage, the Shattered Hymn, the Rings, the Fallen Star and their like) are never lost. Lose the fight, flee it, or have the world stop in the middle of it, and they come back to whoever offered them, straight into their pack or as soon as they return. They do not burn and never vanish from the ground, and every hunter who fought a great enemy takes their own.
Nor do you lose what you carry when a great enemy kills you: fall inside the fight and you wake with your pack, your trinkets and your experience, and leave no grave behind.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rival_hu: Other hunters work these roads too: in a leather jacket, a flannel shirt or a long coat, with a sawn-off shotgun loaded with rock salt, a machete and a flask of holy water. To a human they are friends, and they will help you against demons. To an angel or a demon they are death: they come by night, shoot from range, close in with the machete and throw holy water at whatever has black eyes.
What they carry: salt, holy water, and once in a while a bullet for the Colt.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.0: Three hundred years a witch, thrown out of the Grand Coven for being better than them, and not shy about it. She will not fight you in her own house. Talk to her.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.1: She teaches for a price, copying Witchcraft pages out for you herself: five at most on offer, the lowest tier first, only pages you do not know and your Witchcraft mastery lets you learn. A first-tier page costs eight emeralds; a second-tier one sixteen, two gold ingots and two amethyst shards; a third-tier one twenty-four, four gold and a ghast tear. A Master's page she keeps for her allies, and only one: see Unmark.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.2: Every page you buy earns a little of her trust, and some pages she keeps for those she trusts: her own Familiar Bond only after five. She also sells three taglocks for three emeralds, and Witchcraft hexed ink for six.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena.3: She hears things. Ask her the right question at the right time, and she may tell you where to find someone you would rather not meet.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena_a: When the Grand Witch's last phase begins, Rowena comes out of her own smoke beside you. Nothing touches her. She keeps near the hunters, throws a bolt at the coven every five seconds, and when the Grand Witch takes everyone's lock of hair she draws the green circles to stand in.
When it is over she watches the Grand Witch fall, and goes home. That is where she will take the Mark off you.
Rowena, on your side for once
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowena_b: Only for the one who kept the Book. Read it in her house at night, within the twelve-block ring round the middle of her house (or a few blocks past it), and she steps out of yellow smoke. Her house is the arena, and it is put back as it was afterwards. Three phases, a third of her strength each.
The Witch at Home: a flick of the wrist down a violet lane that throws whoever is in it; Ignis, a red circle where you stand and then fire; Glacies, a blue one, and frost that slows you to a crawl.

The Familiar and the Hexed: a raven answers her and goes for a lock of your hair. While it holds one, every six seconds she sends a curse down it, pain or frailty, wherever you hide. Kill the raven and the lock drops; she calls another twenty seconds later. Her hexed victims shamble at you: kill one and she heals four parts in a hundred; free it with Break Hex or a salt round and it costs her three. Yellow smoke where she is about to appear: step out of it.

The Recitation: she rises into the air and recites over three bowls for fifteen seconds. Smash them: three blows each. Break all three and she drops, stunned for five seconds and taking half as much again. Leave any whole and for the last three seconds the whole house glows red; then the hex sweeps it, twelve for every bowl still standing.
When she falls the Grand Witch walks out of the smoke for whoever kept the Book. Read it again while sneaking, in her house at night, for a rematch.
What she leaves: her Grimoire and her bust the first time (a bust in a rematch)
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rowenas_: "R. MacLeod. Spells, Hexes, Discretion." An embossed card in green ink, taken off a coven witch. The ink is not quite dry, and it never will be: it runs toward its owner's door.
Use it in the Overworld and it tells you which way the ink runs and roughly how far. Anywhere else the ink only pools. No ordinary map leads to her house.

With Lucifer back in his box, Rowena told me where Cain is. The Father of Murder, the first demon-killer and the first Knight of Hell, keeps bees now: a little farm out where the roads give up, honey and silence.

Her own book, left to whoever beats her the first time: a tier IV catalyst. It remembers the last aimed spell you spoke at a spell bowl while you carried it (a curse, a binding, a banishing: anything that needs a target, never a brew) and what named its target.

Use it and it speaks that spell again, at once, with no bowl and no recitation, for the spell's usual mana, at most once a minute. Nothing from the remembered bowl is spent. Hold a taglock or a vial of bound blood in your other hand and it aims at them instead. If the spell finds nothing to act on, it does not count.

Somewhere between twelve hundred and thirty-two hundred blocks from the middle of the world, where a forest meets open ground, stands a house far nicer than it has any right to be: a garden, a library, a workroom with a spell bowl. Every world has exactly one.
Its owner is home whenever a hunter is about. She would like you to wipe your boots.
A House at the Forest's Edge
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.rubys_kn: An iron sword, two demon blood and a hellfire ember on the altar of a blood circle. It cuts demons deeper than steel should.
A demon slain with it always bleeds: the blood is yours every time, smoke or no smoke. Cold iron, too, so it scatters a ghost. Later it is the key to something worse.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.runes.0: A blank rune is smooth stone, chalk and Enochian ink. Carve it at a small circle: the offerings on the altar, the blank in your hand to light it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.runes.1: For blades: Edge cuts deeper (a tenth of the blade's damage, at least a point and a half), Ember sets alight, Frost slows, Leech heals you from what you deal, Swiftness quickens your swing. For catalysts: Resonance makes spells cheaper and harder, Focus brings them back faster, Echo makes them repeat now and then. Sanctity fits anything and makes every blow holy.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.runes.2: Two runes come only from the great ones. Void, from what the Darkness leaves, carved at night: it drinks the light, and only a tier IV weapon will take it. Hymn, from the Chorus's shards: every fourth blow or spell rings out again as holy light.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.0: Salt is your first friend. Rock salt shows up in the stone like any ore, deeper as deepslate. No ore nearby? Boil a bucket of water dry in a furnace.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.1: Pour it on the ground as a line. You can walk over it; a demon cannot. It is a wall to them, solid as stone, and they will walk the long way round rather than test it. A ghost cannot cross it either.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.2: Salt will not stop the great ones. Nothing you pour on the floor holds a boss. Keep a stack on you anyway: the exorcism, the binding, the bones of a restless grave and half the bowl spells want it.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt.cap: Rock salt, in stone and deepslate
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.salt_and: A lonely graveyard, one to three graves on flat dry ground, headstones and mounds of grave soil. Only one of them is restless. Its bones lie two blocks under the end of the mound by the headstone.

Dig the soil and the dirt under it until the bones are bare; while the spirit is restless, they will not break. Salt them. Then set them alight with flint and steel or a fire charge. The ghost goes with them, for good. A Banishing does the same from the bowl.
One grave in each yard hides a chest under the foot of its mound. Grave dirt from the mounds goes into hex bags and darker work.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.seraph_w: Six wings, what is left of the Broken Chorus when it is silenced. Worn on the back (Curios), they rest, fold when you crouch, and open wide when you fall.
They will not carry you anywhere. They are only for show, and what a show.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.shapeshi: It wears somebody else: a villager at the edge of town, or, on a case, the face of a hunter you know. In its borrowed skin it shrugs off most of what you do to it.
Weakness: silver, or a true sight (Second Sight, or the Spellwright's Spectacles), shows it for what it is. Found out, its skin sloughs off and it takes every blow in full.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_ef: The effects are what the spell does. You cannot draw the same one twice in a spell.

Smite is holy force, twice as hard on demons and the dead. Hellfire burns flesh and a pinch of sulfur. Frost slows, freezes, and turns still water to ice. Mend closes wounds and smothers flames. Repel throws the target away from you. Reveal strips invisibility, outlines what it touches and unmasks illusions.

Two are a hunter's sigils. Exorcise is agony to a demon, and casts a trapped one out entirely; it burns salt. The Snare (once called Bind) holds a demon for a breath, two seconds, as a devil's trap would, and roots anything else to the spot for as long. It is a moment's grace, not a cage: paint a trap for the real holding.

A spell written with the old Bind still works: every page, scroll and formula that names it casts the Snare. Each effect belongs to one of the four schools, and the first effect decides the spell's (see The Four Schools).
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_fo: A spell is a form, up to three effects and up to three modifiers. The form is how it reaches the world.

Touch takes whatever is within arm's reach; a helpful spell with nothing there falls back on you. Bolt is thrown and flies straight until it hits something. Burst is a pulse outward from you. Ward is a circle at your feet that keeps working and stops hostile projectiles.
Touch and Bolt are cheap and quick. Burst and Ward cost more and your hand needs longer to recover. Ward is the harder sigil to come by, and the one you will want when something big starts to glow.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_mo: Modifiers bend a spell and multiply its cost. Empower makes the effects stronger. Extend makes them last longer and reach further. Widen spreads them over an area.
Echo makes the spell repeat itself a moment later. It is written in a hand no one can follow until they are an Adept in some school, or carry Morningstar's Spark. Lucifer carries a page of it.
The Scriptorium shows the cost of a spell as you build it. Watch it: three modifiers on a Burst will empty you in one cast.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigil_pa: Demons carry scraps of their masters' grimoires. Kill one and now and then a torn sigil page falls out of it; occultists carry them far more often than the black-eyed brawlers. Read a page to learn its sigil for good.

The harder pages are written in a hand that burns your eyes. A second-tier page wants an Apprentice of its school, a third-tier one an Adept, a Master's page a Master; a page of no school (a form, a modifier) wants that rank in any school. Keep the ones you cannot read yet: see Mastery. Morningstar's Spark reads them like an Adept.
The Scriptorium keeps an encyclopedia of every sigil: the ones you know, and the shapes of the ones you do not.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sigils_o: Three Enochian effects are found where the choir once sang: Radiance and Halo in the temples of the Hymnal Spires, and in their vaults, one time in three, Judgement.
Radiance (second tier) is a blinding flash: a little harm, two and a half times that on the unholy, three seconds of blindness and five of a glowing outline. A boss only takes the burn.
Halo (second tier) is helpful: a ring of golden hearts that soaks up harm for fifteen seconds. It never touches a foe.

Judgement is a Master's sigil and costs a holy water. It marks the ground under its target; a moment and a half later a column of light falls there and every foe within two and a half blocks takes 16 harm, half as much again if unholy. Whatever moved away in time is spared.
Radiance
Halo
Judgement
Sigils of Heaven
Crowley's Corridors keep the Infernal pages: their chests hold Brimstone, Hellchain and, more rarely, Soul Rend.
Brimstone (second tier) burns a pinch of sulfur and leaves a cloud of burning sulphur where it lands: five pulses of hellfire a second apart, on every foe within two blocks of that spot.
Hellchain (second tier) is a chain of hellfire that burns the target and drags it to you. A boss is too heavy to drag: it only burns.
Soul Rend (third tier) tears at the soul for 5 harm, and you drink half of what it actually does.
Brimstone
Hellchain
Soul Rend
Sigils of Hell
Witchcraft written as sigils. Old graves give up Hex and Pain; Glamour is shelved in the bunker library.
Hex (first tier) lays a jinx for fifteen seconds. Bosses shrug it off, and a protection bag or a Ward of the Name turns it away.
Pain (second tier) is harm that goes straight through armour, and a limp: Slowness for three seconds. A boss takes the harm and no more.

Glamour (third tier) is helpful: you, or a friend, turn unseen for five seconds, and every creature hunting you within sixteen blocks sees an enemy in the nearest other creature instead, or loses the scent. Bosses are never fooled.
Hex
Pain
Glamour
Sigils of the Craft
Plain hunter's work. Salt Shot turns up in graves; Silver Edge in the bunker library.
Salt Shot (first tier) burns a salt: a blast of rock salt that scatters a ghost, breaks a possession and hits a demon two and a half times as hard, knocking it back. Anything else is only stung.

Silver Edge (second tier) lays three charges on your hands for a minute: the next three blows of whatever you hold, even a bare fist, count as silver against werewolves and shapeshifters. Each blow that lands spends one.
Salt Shot
Silver Edge
Sigils of the Hunt
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.silver_m: Three iron ingots, a salt and a holy water in a small circle. Cheap, and made for one thing.
Strikes from behind are double criticals, and a kill from behind takes the head. Get behind them.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.spell_bo: Older than sigils and slower: witchcraft, the way Bobby did it. Five copper ingots and a gold one make the bowl. Set it on solid ground.

Pour in up to four bottles and drop in up to eight ingredients, nothing spare: the mix has to be exactly what the spell asks for. Light it with flint and steel or a fire charge, then speak the Latin before the fire dies. Typing errors cost time; accents and spaces do not matter.
A mix no spell answers to blows up in your face: black smoke, a burn, something nasty for a while, and everything in the bowl is lost. Words you never learned do nothing at all.
Sneak with empty hands to lift the bowl, contents and all. It takes both hands, and it spills if you jump, fall or get hit. Put in your pack, it keeps everything.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.spell_pa: You cannot cast what you do not know the words to. Loose pages with a spell written out, Latin and all, turn up in old graves and forgotten chests, and demons carry them: occultists more often than the black-eyed kind.
A master librarian will sell you one for emeralds and a book. And a crossroads demon who comes back angry always has one on it.
Read a page to learn its spell, with every recipe for it; the page is used up. Once you know a spell, this journal keeps its recipes for you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.spell_sc: Any spell you can compose you can write out in full on a scroll: a sheet of paper and a vial of Enochian ink each. The Scriptorium writes them in batches if you have the paper and ink for it.
A scroll is read aloud once and burns up. Anyone can read one, sigils known or not, and it costs half the mana the spell would. Hand them to whoever hunts with you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sucrocor: Biggerson's new menu, the Turducken Slammer above all, is very filling and laced with SucroCorp's additive. Whoever eats it is sedated for minutes: slow, unable to run, and blind to a Leviathan's borrowed face.
The Leviathans leave sedated people alone: cattle are not hunted, only fattened. Milk or a splash of holy water clears the head.
The Board holds its seat in the SucroCorp skyscraper. Lobby security wears human faces and admits no friendly hunters. This is a stronghold with a reception desk, not a public office.

Above the lobby lie laboratories with vats of black goo, the food line, a vault and the executive floor. Follow the business upwards and you reach the boardroom at the top. Everything below it exists to keep the table supplied.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.sulfur_p: The Pit's clergy. It hangs back and throws balls of burning sulfur; corner it and it whirls its censer into a cloud of smoke that blinds and poisons. Close the distance fast, and don't stand in the cloud.
It serves its side's chain of command: in the strongholds, in the escorts of its officers, and now and then as an officer itself.
A sulfur priest, censer in hand
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.taglocks: A twist of paper and string. Use a blank taglock on a creature or a player to snip a lock of their hair; sneak and use it in the air to take your own.
Snipping is quiet but not invisible: one time in four they notice. A beast turns on you; a person is told someone tugged at their hair, and by whom.

In the bowl a filled taglock names whom the spell is for, as a dose of someone's blood does, and no recipe counts it as an ingredient: drop it in beside the rest. If someone's blood is poured in as well, the blood speaks first.
Locating a person: water, and their blood poured in or their taglock
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_arse: Every blade and catalyst worth carrying is forged by ritual, not at a crafting table, and each has a tier, from I to IV, and room for one to three runes. The tier sets what graving them costs.
Catalysts are held opposite a grimoire, in the other hand, and change your spells; alone, they have a spell of their own. The heavier weapons are swung by charging: hold use, then let go.
Holy weapons count as holy wherever they land. That matters more than their edge against the things at the end of this book.
None of them, as forged, is enough for the great enemies. Each can be ascended at the Hellforge with the shards those enemies leave, tier by tier, up to V (see Ascension).
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_bunk: Out in open country, three to five thousand blocks from the world's heart, a little stone hut sits on a hillside that nobody looks at twice. Behind its steel door, iron stairs go down into the Men of Letters' bunker. Henry's map marks it; no compass will.

Only the Bunker Key opens the vault door. Below: the war room with its war table, the library with its research desks and archive shelves, a lab, a dungeon with a devil's trap painted on the floor, an armoury, a garage and the dormitories. Its desks, its door and its table yield only to members.

The key is needed only once. Turn it in the door and the door remembers you: from then on it opens to your hand, key or no key. Henry hands a spare only to a member who lost theirs before ever getting in.
The war room and the library
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_cage: At the heart of Hell, at its very centre, the Pit falls sheer to the lava sea. Over it, on its chains, hangs the Cage, and under the Cage an island with a dais and four old stones.
Lucifer waits inside, in chains, head bowed. Now and then he looks up at whoever has come so far. Nothing can touch him while the Cage is shut.
The iris in its floor opens only for the four rings and the Key. When it does, he comes down.

Nothing the Cage is made of can be broken: Enochian bars and posts, heavy chains made fast to wall anchors, carved pillars with their capitals and bases, abyssal bricks and flagstones, hellfire braziers, seal lanterns, and the fallen watchers, angels of stone kneeling in their chains.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_choi: Abaddon is dead and her Book is in my pack. Somewhere in it is the cure for the Mark of Cain, and only a witch can read it. I know exactly one witch who would not kill me on sight.

Take it to Rowena and speak of it. She will ask for it. Give it to her and she is in your debt, and against her old sisters of the Grand Coven she will stand with you. Keep it and she will not forgive you: she will want it back, and she will take it if she can.
Either way it is final. You choose once, for good, and a second copy of the Book changes nothing.
What to Do with the Book
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_colt: A Paterson revolver, 1836, five chambers. Samuel Colt made it for one job. There's nothing this gun can't kill. Lucifer carries it, loaded, and leaves it when he falls.

One round kills any living thing outright: any demon, monster, shade, echo or illusion, any beast. Not a hunter (unless the server allows it), and not archangels or anything above them. Against a great enemy it strikes a tenth of its full strength that no armour blunts (the Author, under a third of that), though it will not carry them past one of their turning points. Use to fire; sneak-use or the reload key seats one round at a time.
The rounds cannot be crafted. Once you have held the Colt, forge them by night in a blood circle, eight at a time. A few lie in the Hymnal Spire's temple, and with the great ones when they fall.
Some hunters write their own rules. The Endless Colt is the same gun, always loaded: it never spends a round and never needs reloading. No rite or grave gives it; it is only found in creative mode.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_deal: What it offers, and what it costs in days before the hounds come. Two more hearts, or twenty-five more mana, yours for good: five days. Everything you dropped at your last death that nobody picked up, or a dead pet back on its feet: seven days.

Something rare from its pockets, bullets, embers, shards and the like: ten days. Knowledge: a map to what hides nearby, a Hymnal Spire or a restless grave, or failing that, a book on how to kill the next great thing you have not killed yet: ten days.
The contract tells you whose soul, for what, and how long you have. Keep it. You will need it if you mean to break the deal.
The contract it leaves in your hands
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_debt: On the last day you will hear the dogs. When it falls due, a pack of three to five hellhounds comes for you, wherever you are. Survive the hunt, by killing the pack or lasting two minutes, and the debt is paid.
Die while they are on you and the debt is paid another way. You come back, but not all of you: for three days you are two hearts short and your mana does not return.

Or break it. Burn the contract in a bowl, with holy water, salt and a hellfire ember, and the demon who holds it walks again, angry. Kill it before your time runs out and the contract is void. If it flees its vessel, it comes back another night.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_dock: Everything in Heaven was written before it happened, and from his third phase Zachariah stops pretending otherwise. The docket on your screen lists what he will do next, in order: three attacks, then five in his last phase. Each one's mark appears on the floor three seconds early. Read it and stand where it isn't.
It is honest, almost. Once a phase he revises it: one line is struck through, and a moment later something else takes its place.

The Termination Notice is the one to fear. The hunter it names is smitten five seconds later for two fifths of their strength, unless they stand at one of the desks that are safe from it, or share it: everyone within three blocks of them takes a part of the blow.
Pass his test and he types your ending. "The End" is the chronicle of your hunt as he saw it: the enemies you beat, what you killed, the deals you made. Use it to read.

The Author's Pen rewrites a small corner of the world. Sneak and use it to choose: the land (the biome around the block you touch), the sky (clear day, rain, storm, clear night) or a creature (into another of its kind; never a great enemy, never a person). Every rewrite takes a long while to dry.

Sam's amulet, worn as a necklace (or in hand without Curios), gives four hearts and shows you the powerful - great enemies and the strange things of this world - through walls, and shines when one is near.
These are given once to each hunter, for their first victory. He will gladly fight you again - another draft - but for you the props department is closed.
The End, the Pen, the amulet
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_mark: Taken from Cain as he dies, or later at his grave, it burns into the forearm. Every Knight of Hell bears it, and the Knight's rite will not take a Prince who does not already.

The Mark thirsts. For five minutes after a kill it rests; then its Thirst climbs a hundredth every minute. Every kill slakes it, a hundredth for each soul the victim was worth (two at least, thirty at most), and Cain's honey takes a quarter off. The more it thirsts, the less healing does: at its worst, only half.

From half Thirst you are in bloodlust: your blows land a fifth harder, it whispers, and a demon's Corruption drains and will not come back. At full it feeds on you, a point of health every ten seconds. Die at full Thirst as a human, or as an angel whose grace it burns out, and you do not stay dead: you rise a demon, and the Thirst is left at half.

The First Blade answers it: in a Marked hand it strikes three times as hard and never hungers, for the Mark's Thirst takes the blade's place. A Mark that was ever taken off and is taken again remembers the way: it comes back already at half.
There is a cure in the Book of the Damned, if a witch will read it for you: see Unmark. A Knight whose Mark is taken off stays a Knight.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_mess: At the first dawn after you first bring Azazel down, an angel comes to you: a tired man in a trench coat, with the shadow of wings behind him. He cannot be hurt, and he only wants to talk. He offers you Grace.

Hear him out and he gives you a Vial of Grace and the way to take it in. Turn him away and he comes back three dawns later. Once heeded he no longer comes on his own, but a spell at the bowl can call him again. He never comes to a demon.
An angel in a borrowed trench coat
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.the_tric: Ever since Lucifer went back in his box, little things have been happening. A candy wrapper by your feet when you haven't eaten any candy. A party hat on a cow. A laugh track somewhere out of sight. A villager quoting a soap opera. A chest that opens and shuts on its own, with nothing missing from it.

None of it breaks anything, takes anything or hurts anyone, and it never happens more than once a day. That is how you know it is not a ghost: it's a Trickster, a pagan god of mischief who plays his jokes on the people who deserve them, and he has noticed you.

Notice three of his pranks and you're on his trail. He can't resist sweets: cook a bait for him in a small circle with three sugar, a honey bottle, cocoa beans, holy oil and a gold nugget, lit with flint and steel.
What he leaves lying around, and what he can't resist
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.training: Naomi tests her work. Copies rise on the training floor: some kneel with their hands up, wearing the faces of people you would never hurt (Dean, Sam, Castiel, a pet you lost, you yourself); the others are hunters with demons' black eyes, and they come for you.

Strike a kneeling copy and the test has worked: you are Conditioned for ten seconds (your blows against angels fall soft) and she heals. Kill every hostile copy within fifteen seconds without touching one that kneels, and the result is unexpected: she is stunned for three seconds and takes more from every blow.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.trickste: His candy, in a striped wrapper. Eat one and something happens for a little while: always something good, or at least nothing bad. You never know which. That is the point.

His remote control. Point it at a creature and change its channel: it might shrink for a while, turn up in a silly costume, or become another creature of its size altogether. It needs half a minute between uses, and it never works on a great enemy, a named creature or a villager with a trade.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.trophies: Every great one leaves its likeness behind, a little statue to set on a shelf and remember the night by.
Do not get too attached to three of them. War wants Lucifer's, Famine the Darkness's and Pestilence the Chorus's.
Watch the corner of your eye: when the static clears, the channel's number is there, and every channel has its own rule. The banner at the top is his health; the sign under it is the studio's.

CH 2, the Sitcom. A living room, a staircase, doors, and an audience. While the LAUGH sign is lit he can't be touched and plays his gags: pies in the face that blind you, banana peels, a piano from the ceiling (watch for its shadow), extras through the doors. When the sign goes dark he takes more from every blow. Keep hitting him: if nobody touches him for a few seconds, the APPLAUSE sign lights and the audience heals him.

CH 5, Nutcracker! A Japanese game show over a pit of foam: three platforms, red, blue and yellow. Every so often a question appears with three answers, one on each colour. Stand on the right platform before the buzzer: you come away stronger and he is stunned for a moment. Stand on a wrong one, or none, and the trap door or the giant mallet finds you. Fight him between the rounds. The questions are about everything in this book.

CH 7, Dr. Sexy, M.D. A hospital ward with a giant heart monitor. Strike him on the beep (the trace on your screen spikes; the lit band in its middle is your moment) and the blow is critical. The beat quickens as the episode goes on. The defibrillator shocks marked zones of the floor; and nurses, doubles of him in caps, walk to him to heal him: one blow stops a nurse.

CH 9, A Word from Our Sponsor. A white stage with five podiums and five spokesmen, all of him; only the real one casts a shadow of six golden wings. Strike a double and the joke is on you, and the podiums shuffle. They shuffle when you strike the real one too, and every ten seconds. Watch the floor, not the faces.

A human's free will sees through his tricks a little: in the commercial, one more double flickers and fades for them. Demons are cast as the episode's villain and take more from him; an angel's grace drains in his commercial breaks, little brother.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.unmark.0: The cure for the Mark of Cain, out of the Book of the Damned. Only a witch who outlived your witch fight can work it: Rowena if you gave her the Book and the Grand Witch fell, the Grand Witch if you kept it and Rowena fell. The price is a vial of your own bound blood.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.unmark.1: The simple way is to ask her. Rowena does it in her house; the Grand Witch wherever she stands, reading from the Book you kept, so carry it. Either takes the vial from your pack.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.unmark.2: Or speak it at a bowl yourself, with the witch within eight blocks of it and, if you kept the Book, the Book on you (it is not spent). Dragon's breath, honey and holy water; your bound blood, an echo shard, an amethyst shard and a ghast tear; a hundred and fifty mana. It is a Master's page found in no chest: Rowena sells it only to an ally who saw the Grand Witch fall, for thirty-two emeralds, eight gold and an echo shard.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.unmarked: The Mark is gone. My arm is just an arm. The First Blade is just a very old bone.
If I was a Knight of Hell I still am: the rank stays, the Thirst does not. Nobody will put the Mark back on me behind my back.
Cain's grave would still give it to me if I asked. It would come back hungry, half-way to bloodlust from the first day. I am not going to ask.
Rowena would say I owe her. She would be right. She usually is.
Pale, quick and hungry, they nest in barns and mines and keep to the dark. When they feed a second row of teeth slides down over the first, and a bite leaves you bleeding.

Weakness: only a beheading keeps one down. Kill it with a sword, an axe or a silver machete in your hand, or it goes down and rises again ten seconds later. Dead man's blood (used on it, or smeared on a blade held in your other hand) stuns it cold. Brew it from glass bottles, rotten flesh, a bone and redstone.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.vitality: Every great enemy you outlive makes you harder to kill. The first time each of them falls, everyone who fought it gains two hearts of health for good; the Trickster, who was only playing, gives one. Dying does not take them back.
By the time you knock on the Author's door you will carry twenty-five more hearts than you started with. You will need every one.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.war.0: A man in a red suit with a sword at his hip, who makes neighbours kill each other for fun. Once Lucifer has fallen, call him in a great circle with iron swords, demon blood and gunpowder, lit with flint and steel.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.war.1: He lays a battlefield over the arena: trenches, wire, craters. His sword comes in combos he shows you first. Raise a shield just as a blow lands and he staggers: for three seconds he takes half again as much.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.war.2: Then his four standards rise. Every blow he takes and every standard left standing makes him angrier, faster and harder-hitting; break them. And he gets into your head: for a while every other hunter looks like a demon, and mirages walk the field, some hostile, some innocent. The innocent never strike and kneel where they stand. Hit an innocent or a friend and the blow comes back on you.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.war.3: At the end he mounts his red horse and charges across the field, sweeping his sword, setting the trenches alight.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.war_tabl: Set nine map table pieces down in a square and they lock together into a war table: dark glass with a projector under it, and over the glass a hologram of the land for a mile and more around, its hills and rivers and seas. Where the land has been seen, the picture is sharp; where it has only been foretold, it flickers. Break any piece and the table comes apart.
Your cases are on it: the open one as a red light with a line run to it from the table, the closed ones dim. Look at the glass and it tells you what you are looking at and how far it is.
Use the table to open it. Drag the map, zoom it, ask for a case and read its brief. Double-click the map to stick a pin in it: the pins belong to the table, and everyone who uses it sees them.

A Letters compass points at your open case. Carry one to the table and you can set it on any pin instead (and back on the case). Use it to hear what it points at and how far; sneak and use it to let a pin go. In an outsider's hand, with no case, or away from the world above, its needle only spins.

A case can be abandoned there too. It is filed as gone cold, and the order gives you no other before the next dawn. The bunker's table stands in its war room; researching the order's cartography gives you the blueprint to build another anywhere in the world above. The blueprint comes back out of the crafting grid.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.warded_r: A circle broken mid-rite lashes out: thunder, a burn, and now and then something comes through. Cast a Ward of your own over the altar before you light it and the Ward takes the backlash: no burn, and nothing answers. The rite is still lost, and so are its offerings.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.werewolf: By day a lean, unshaven man who keeps to himself. At night his bones crack and he turns into a hulking wolf with yellow eyes, strongest under a full moon.
Weakness: silver, and only silver, ends it. Anything else drives it off at the last; it flees, licks its wounds and comes back whole.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.wild_bar: Better wishes, worse prices. Besides everything the bowl's demon offers, a wild one can raise the weapon in your hand one tier of Ascension (never past the fourth, nor past what you have earned); give you the trophies of up to three great enemies you have already beaten, with a shard for each; bring back the last pet you lost, collar or not; or lift a curse: a hungry weapon's, Heaven's Mark, the hollowness of a soul taken, or a jinx.

The price: half the usual days before the hounds come, the soul clause already ticked, and a bigger pack (five to seven) that you must outlast for three minutes, not two. Sealing one is a Wild Bargain.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.wild_cro: The bowl is the quick way. The old way still works, out where two dirt roads meet in open country, far from any town: a weathered marker, a dead tree, and in the very middle a patch of loose, dark soil that nothing grows on.

Fill a crossroads box: a bone, grave soil, paper, sulfur and an iron nugget. Bury it in that soil at night and stay close: a few moments later the demon comes up the road, and no bowl or contract is asked of you. A crossroads takes one box from you a night; walk off before it comes and the box is wasted.
A wild demon offers more than the one in the bowl, and charges more for it (Wild Bargains, in this book).
The box, and where it goes
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.witch_co: Binding of the Name roots whoever the bowl names for twenty seconds, if they are within two hundred and fifty-six blocks in this world. A boss is never held, though one or two can be checked for a breath.

Banish by Name sends the named away as the banishing rites would: a ghost laid to rest, a demon or a hound cast back into the dark, a lesser angel sent home, a demon player expelled (it hurts, and burns their Corruption away), an angel player flung far. Never a boss, never a crossroads demon (only its death breaks a deal), never anything of this world.
Compel makes a creature, the named one or else the nearest within eight blocks of the bowl, follow you and spare you for a minute. A named player is drawn slowly toward the bowl for five seconds.

Break Hex frees the named, or you, of every curse of the craft (jinx, bleeding, agony, rot, silence, marks, compulsion, bad luck) and burns the curse bags within eight blocks of the bowl and of them, and any they carry.

Deep in swamps, dark forests and old taiga, the witches gather: three huts round a ring of standing stones and a working spell bowl, bones in the grass. Two to four hedge witches keep it with their familiars; in about a third of them a coven witch leads. Their victims shuffle at the edges.
Go in with salt and something to turn a curse. Burn the familiars first; break the coven witch's bubble before you waste blows on it.
The bowl is real, and yours to use once its keepers are gone.
Their chests: pages, taglocks, hexed ink, blood, bags
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.witch_cu: A curse is aimed. Put something of your victim's in the bowl with the rest: a dose of their blood poured in beyond what the spell asks for, or a taglock of their hair. Without it the bowl will not catch. With it, the curse finds them anywhere in the world, so long as they are somewhere awake.

It is refused by the great ones, every boss, and by other hunters unless the world allows them to fight each other. A Ward of the Name turns it away: the curse fails and you take a heart and a half for trying. A Mirror Hex sends it back on you, once.
Agony hurts every two seconds but, like poison, never kills. Break Hex lifts any of them.
Misfortune: bad luck and a jinx, five minutes
Frailty: weakness, slow hands, and a fifth more harm, two minutes
Rot: hunger, a little poison, and the food in their pack rots, two minutes
Silence: no sigils and no powers, a minute
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.witch_tr: Locate Being is the Locating spell for anyone at all, player or creature: water, a compass, string and salt, and something of theirs.

Scrying shows you in the smoke where they are in this world: the land they stand in and roughly where, and it outlines them for thirty seconds for everyone to see. A Ward of the Name veils its bearer.
Trace the Familiar needs nothing of anyone's: the smoke leads to the nearest witch, or a witch's bound familiar, within a hundred and sixty blocks.
journal.supernaturalcraft.entry.zacharia: Heaven's middle management: a balding angel in a grey suit who believes in procedure and in nothing else. Every prophecy has a form, every form has a cabinet, and every hunter is a file he would like to close.

Once Naomi has fallen, the lift at the back of her room goes up to his office: rows of desks and cubicles under flat white light, and they do not end. Walk far enough in any direction and you come back in from the other side. He does not need to walk: he blinks. Nobody else's road needs him.
Everyone in his office does paperwork. He hands each of you a Heavenly Form, and while you hold one that is not filed, your blows are worth a quarter. File it (Heavenly Forms, in this book).

I. Intake. A storm of memos in a cone. A rubber stamp slams a square of floor: DENIED, and your wounds stop closing for a while. Clerks come to help him. He strikes where you stand now, and again where you stood three seconds ago. He hands one of you a Termination Notice.
II. Review. The cubicles shuffle round you and block your sight; he reassigns you across the office.
III. It Was Already Written. His six wings open, and they buffet. From now on he tells you what comes next: read the docket (The Docket, in this book).
IV. Final Judgment. The office comes apart, there is only a golden sky, and he smites Heaven itself in lines of gold that run out from him: find the ring of safe floor between them.
Once he has fallen, the lift carries you up to an empty office. Crouch as you ride it to call him back.
Met again, he leaves his bust, and now and then his blade or his seal. Like every great enemy, he also leaves a shard and, the first time, a heart. His fall makes your house in Heaven your home.
What he leaves the first time

An ornate silver angel blade, a holy weapon of the fourth tier. Every third blow files its target: for three seconds it takes a quarter more from everything. Raise it at the Hellforge and the filing bites deeper.

I understand. It is a great deal to ask of anyone.
I'll call again in a few days. Do try to stay alive until then.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.offer.1: Good morning. Forgive the hour, and the intrusion. My name is Henry Winchester.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.offer.2: I am a Legacy of the Men of Letters: a brotherhood of scholars who studied the things that go bump in the night, so that men like you could put them down.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.offer.3: Word travels, even to us. You stood against the Devil himself, and you walked away. That is not luck. That is a hunter.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.offer.4: We kept our knowledge in a bunker in open country, built to outlast anything. It has sat locked for far too long.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.offer.5: I am offering you a place among us: the key, the library, the war room, and every secret we ever wrote down. Will you take it?
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.offer_aga: Good morning again. I did say I would come back, and a Winchester keeps his word.
The offer stands. The archive does not read itself, and the things out there are not waiting for us to make up our minds.
So: will you take up the Legacy?
Ah, there you are. Pull up a chair.
The map table never sleeps: missing persons, strange deaths, cattle drained of blood. Somebody has to look into them.
Shall I give you a case?
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.welcome.1: Splendid. Then welcome to the Men of Letters, Aspirant.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.welcome.2: Here is the key. Don't lose it; there is only the one, and the door was built to keep out worse than burglars.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.welcome.3: And a map. The bunker lies out in the open country, beneath a little stone hut that nobody ever looks at twice.
legacy.supernaturalcraft.henry.welcome.4: I'll be waiting for you in the war room, by the map table. Read everything. Then we'll talk about cases.
